## CLUI TUI Project Structure Analysis

I've thoroughly explored the clui project at `/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/clui`. This is a **TypeScript/React terminal UI** (not Rust) built with Ink 6 and React 19. Here's the complete breakdown:

### 1. MAIN LAYOUT COMPONENT

**Layout Dimensions:**
- Terminal height: Retrieved dynamically from `useStdout().rows`
- Sidebar width: **24 characters** (default, configurable)
- Center area: Flexible growth (`flexGrow={1}`) to fill remaining space
- Structure: Row-based (`flexDirection="row"`) with fixed-width sidebars flanking a flexible center

### 2. SIDEBAR IMPLEMENTATIONS

#### Session Sidebar
**File:** `/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/clui/src/shell/components/SessionSidebar.tsx`

<Box flexDirection="column" padding={1}>

### 5. BORDER & BOX DRAWING CHARACTERS

**Ink's borderStyle values used:**
- `"single"` — Standard light box-drawing characters:
  - Horizontal: `─`
  - Vertical: `│`
  - Corners: `┌ ┐ └ ┘`
  - Junctions: `├ ┤ ┬ ┴ ┼`
  
- `"double"` — Heavy/double characters (used only in WorktreePrompt):
  - Horizontal: `═`
  - Vertical: `║`
  - Corners: `╔ ╗ ╚ ╝`
  - Junctions: `╠ ╣ ╦ ╩ ╬`

**Colors used:**
- Borders: `"gray"` (except WorktreePrompt which uses `"yellow"`)
- Text: green, white, cyan, yellow, red, magenta, blue, gray

### 6. RESIZE AND INTERACTION SUPPORT

**No native mouse/resize support exists in the codebase.** However:

**Keyboard interactions implemented:**
- **Tab navigation:** Ctrl+T (new), Ctrl+W (close), Ctrl+1-9 (switch tabs), Tab/Shift+Tab (cycle)
- **Sidebar toggles:** Ctrl+H (sessions), Ctrl+S (skills)
- **Context management:** Ctrl+R (reset), Ctrl+Shift+S (snapshot)
- **Session sidebar:** Arrow keys (navigate), Enter (open), r (rename), c (cycle color)
- **Skills sidebar:** 1/2/3 (toggle tiers)
- **Compact detail:** x (expand/collapse)
- **Worktree prompt:** k (keep), c (cleanup), Esc (cancel)

**All UI interactions are keyboard-driven via Ink's `useInput()` hook.** There is no mouse support or dynamic resizing of sidebars/columns.

### 7. KEY COMPONENT FILES SUMMARY

| Component | File | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| **Layout** | `Layout.tsx` | Main 3-column flex container |
| **SessionSidebar** | `SessionSidebar.tsx` | Left sidebar (24px), session list + filter |
| **SkillsSidebar** | `SkillsSidebar.tsx` | Right sidebar (24px), 3-tier skill browser |
| **ChatView** | `ChatView.tsx` | Center area, scrolling message history |
| **TabBar** | `TabBar.tsx` | Top of center, tab switching |
| **InputBar** | `InputBar.tsx` | Bottom of center, user input with green `>` prefix |
| **ContextBar** | `ContextBar.tsx` | Above input, sticky/one-shot pins display |
| **StatusBar** | `StatusBar.tsx` | Bottom, metadata display (model, tokens, cost, git) |
| **CompactDetail** | `CompactDetail.tsx` | Context compaction event viewer (red border) |
| **WorktreePrompt** | `WorktreePrompt.tsx` | Worktree cleanup confirmation (double yellow border) |

### 8. TECHNOLOGY STACK

- **UI Framework:** Ink 6.8.0 with React 19.2.4
- **Input:** ink-text-input 6.0.0
- **State Management:** Zustand 5.0.12
- **IPC:** Node.js net (Unix Domain Sockets)
- **Database:** better-sqlite3 12.8.0
- **Build:** tsup, TypeScript 6.0.2

All borders and styling are handled by Ink's declarative props (`borderStyle`, `borderColor`, `flexDirection`, padding, margins, colors). No custom box-drawing code exists.

> AGENT

Good, I have full context now. Let me address your requests with some important technical realities:

**Re: Item 1 — Resizable sidebars via mouse hover/drag:**
Bad idea for this stack. Ink (terminal React) has **no native mouse hover/click-drag support**. Terminal mouse events (`xterm` mouse protocol) are low-level, fragile, and Ink doesn't expose them. Implementing drag-to-resize on sidebar edges would require raw ANSI escape sequence handling — brittle and not worth the effort.

**Better alternative:** Keyboard-driven resize. E.g., `Ctrl+Left/Right` to shrink/grow sidebars by 1-2 columns. Clean, reliable, fits the TUI paradigm. Same UX result with 10x less complexity.

**Re: Item 4 — Border radius:**
Not possible. Terminals render in a character grid. There are no curved box-drawing characters in Unicode. The closest you get is `╭╮╰╯` (rounded corners) — which Ink supports as `borderStyle="round"`. That's the maximum "radius" you'll get in a TUI.

**Items 2 & 3** are straightforward.

So before I design this, one question:

**For sidebar resizing — are you OK with keyboard shortcuts (e.g., `Ctrl+Left/Right`) instead of mouse drag?** Or do you want to explore the mouse route despite the complexity?

just question if we use rust instead of ink for 1st.. will it be better or the same?

> AGENT

Rust TUI libs (ratatui, crossterm) have **first-class mouse support** — hover detection, click coordinates, drag events all built in. So yes, drag-to-resize sidebars would be trivial in Rust.

But you'd be rewriting the entire shell UI. That's not a small change — it's a new project.

**Realistic options:**

1. **Stay Ink, keyboard resize** — 1-2 hours of work, works well
2. **Add raw mouse support to Ink** — possible via `process.stdin` raw mode + ANSI mouse escape parsing. Hacky but doable. ~1 day.
3. **Rewrite shell in Rust** — best mouse/rendering, but weeks of work to recreate what you have

49	  // Create initial tab and spawn its worker

55	      setInitialized(true);
56	    }
57	  }, [initialized, createTab, spawnWorker]);
58	
59	  // Spawn worker when new tab is created (only once per tab)
60	  useEffect(() => {
61	    for (const tab of tabs) {

105	      .replace(/\/\S+/g, "")
106	      .trim();

108	    if (cleanText) {

110	      sendPrompt(activeTabId, cleanText, currentPins);

7	function formatDuration(seconds: number): string {
8	  if (seconds < 60) return `${seconds}s`;
9	  const m = Math.floor(seconds / 60);
10	  const s = seconds % 60;
11	  return s > 0 ? `${m}m${s}s` : `${m}m`;
12	}
13	
14	function formatCost(cost: number): string {
15	  return `$${cost.toFixed(2)}`;
16	}
17	
18	function formatTokens(n: number): string {
19	  if (n >= 1000000) return `${(n / 1000000).toFixed(1)}M`;
20	  if (n >= 1000) return `${(n / 1000).toFixed(1)}k`;
21	  return `${n}`;
22	}

24	function renderField(
25	  key: string,
26	  _label: string,
27	  data: StatusBarData
28	): React.ReactElement | null {
29	  switch (key) {
30	    case "model":
31	      return data.model ? <Text color="green">{data.model}</Text> : null;
32	    case "totalTokens":
33	      return <Text color="yellow">Total: {formatTokens(data.totalTokens)}</Text>;
34	    case "contextTokens":
35	      return <Text color="yellow">Ctx: {formatTokens(data.contextTokens)}</Text>;
36	    case "contextPercent": {
37	      const pct = data.contextPercent;
38	      const color = pct > 80 ? "red" : pct > 50 ? "yellow" : "green";
39	      return <Text color={color}>Ctx: {pct.toFixed(1)}%</Text>;
40	    }
41	    case "cost":
42	      return <Text color="cyan">{formatCost(data.cost)}</Text>;
43	    case "durationSeconds":
44	      return <Text color="magenta">{formatDuration(data.durationSeconds)}</Text>;
45	    case "gitBranch":
46	      return data.gitBranch ? (
47	        <Text color="yellow">@ {data.gitBranch}</Text>
48	      ) : (
49	        <Text color="gray">@ no git</Text>
50	      );
51	    case "gitDiffStats":
52	      if (!data.gitDiffStats) return null;
53	      return (
54	        <Text>
55	          <Text color="green">+{data.gitDiffStats.added}</Text>
56	          <Text> </Text>
57	          <Text color="red">-{data.gitDiffStats.removed}</Text>
58	          <Text> </Text>
59	          <Text color="yellow">~{data.gitDiffStats.modified}</Text>
60	        </Text>
61	      );
62	    case "style":
63	      return data.style ? <Text color="white">Style: {data.style}</Text> : null;
64	    case "sessionId":
65	      return data.sessionId ? <Text color="gray">{data.sessionId.slice(0, 8)}</Text> : null;
66	    default:
67	      return null;
68	  }
69	}

77	export function StatusBar({ fields }: StatusBarProps): React.ReactElement {
78	  const activeTabId = useStore((s) => s.activeTabId);
79	  const allStatus = useStore((s) => s.tabStatus);
80	  const allCompactEvents = useStore((s) => s.tabCompactEvents);
81	
82	  const data = activeTabId ? allStatus[activeTabId] : null;
83	  const compactEvents = (activeTabId && allCompactEvents[activeTabId]) || EMPTY_EVENTS;
84	
85	  const enabledFields = (fields || config.defaultStatusBarFields).filter(
86	    (f) => f.enabled
87	  );
88	
89	  if (!data) {
90	    return (
91	      <Box paddingX={1}>
92	        <Text color="gray">No active session</Text>
93	      </Box>
94	    );
95	  }
96	
97	  const lastCompact = compactEvents[compactEvents.length - 1];
98	
99	  return (
100	    <Box paddingX={1} flexDirection="row" gap={1}>
101	      {enabledFields.map((field) => {
102	        const rendered = renderField(field.key, field.label, data);
103	        if (!rendered) return null;
104	        return (
105	          <React.Fragment key={field.key}>
106	            {rendered}
107	            <Text color="gray"> | </Text>
108	          </React.Fragment>
109	        );
110	      })}
111	      {lastCompact && <Text color="red">* compacted</Text>}
112	    </Box>
113	  );
114	}

5	export function TabBar(): React.ReactElement {
6	  const tabs = useStore((s) => s.tabs);
7	  const activeTabId = useStore((s) => s.activeTabId);
8	  const setActiveTab = useStore((s) => s.setActiveTab);
9	  const createTab = useStore((s) => s.createTab);
10	  const closeTab = useStore((s) => s.closeTab);
11	
12	  useInput((input, key) => {
13	    if (input === "t" && key.ctrl) {
14	      createTab();
15	      return;
16	    }
17	
18	    if (input === "w" && key.ctrl && activeTabId) {
19	      closeTab(activeTabId);
20	      return;
21	    }
22	
23	    if (key.ctrl && input >= "1" && input <= "9") {
24	      const idx = parseInt(input, 10) - 1;
25	      if (tabs[idx]) {
26	        setActiveTab(tabs[idx].id);
27	      }
28	      return;
29	    }
30	
31	    if (key.tab && !key.shift && tabs.length > 1) {
32	      const currentIdx = tabs.findIndex((t) => t.id === activeTabId);
33	      const nextIdx = (currentIdx + 1) % tabs.length;
34	      setActiveTab(tabs[nextIdx].id);
35	    }
36	  });
37	
38	  return (
39	    <Box flexDirection="row" borderStyle="round" borderColor="gray" borderBottom={false}>
40	      {tabs.map((tab) => (
41	        <Box key={tab.id} paddingX={1}>
42	          <Text
43	            color={tab.id === activeTabId ? "cyan" : "gray"}
44	            bold={tab.id === activeTabId}
45	          >
46	            {tab.index}: {tab.name}
47	          </Text>
48	        </Box>
49	      ))}
50	      <Box paddingX={1}>
51	        <Text color="green">[+]</Text>
52	      </Box>
53	    </Box>
54	  );
55	}

  "content": "import { useEffect, useRef, useCallback } from \"react\";\nimport { useStdin } from \"ink\";\n\nexport interface MouseEvent {\n  x: number; // 0-based column\n  y: number; // 0-based row\n  button: \"left\" | \"right\" | \"middle\" | \"none\" | \"scrollUp\" | \"scrollDown\";\n  type: \"press\" | \"release\" | \"move\";\n}\n\ntype MouseHandler = (event: MouseEvent) => void;\n\n/**\n * Enables xterm SGR mouse tracking and emits parsed mouse events.\n * Uses SGR (mode 1006) for coordinates > 223.\n */\nexport function useMouse(onMouse: MouseHandler): void {\n  const { stdin, setRawMode } = useStdin();\n  const handlerRef = useRef(onMouse);\n  handlerRef.current = onMouse;\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (!stdin) return;\n\n    // Enable mouse tracking:\n    // 1000 = basic button tracking\n    // 1002 = button-event tracking (reports motion while pressed)\n    // 1003 = any-event tracking (reports all motion)\n    // 1006 = SGR extended coordinates\n    const enableSeq = \"\\x1b[?1000h\\x1b[?1002h\\x1b[?1006h\";\n    const disableSeq = \"\\x1b[?1006l\\x1b[?1002l\\x1b[?1000l\";\n\n    process.stdout.write(enableSeq);\n\n    let buffer = \"\";\n\n    function parseData(data: Buffer): void {\n      buffer += data.toString(\"utf-8\");\n\n      // SGR mouse format: \\x1b[<Btn;X;Y[Mm]\n      // M = press/motion, m = release\n      const sgrRegex = /\\x1b\\[<(\\d+);(\\d+);(\\d+)([Mm])/g;\n      let match: RegExpExecArray | null;\n      let lastIndex = 0;\n\n      while ((match = sgrRegex.exec(buffer)) !== null) {\n        lastIndex = match.index + match[0].length;\n        const btnCode = parseInt(match[1], 10);\n        const x = parseInt(match[2], 10) - 1; // 1-based → 0-based\n        const y = parseInt(match[3], 10) - 1;\n        const isRelease = match[4] === \"m\";\n\n        const event = parseSgrButton(btnCode, x, y, isRelease);\n        if (event) {\n          handlerRef.current(event);\n        }\n      }\n\n      // Keep only unparsed tail\n      if (lastIndex > 0) {\n        buffer = buffer.slice(lastIndex);\n      }\n\n      // Prevent buffer from growing unbounded\n      if (buffer.length > 256) {\n        buffer = buffer.slice(-64);\n      }\n    }\n\n    stdin.on(\"data\", parseData);\n\n    return () => {\n      stdin.off(\"data\", parseData);\n      process.stdout.write(disableSeq);\n    };\n  }, [stdin]);\n}\n\nfunction parseSgrButton(\n  btnCode: number,\n  x: number,\n  y: number,\n  isRelease: boolean\n): MouseEvent | null {\n  const isMotion = (btnCode & 32) !== 0;\n  const baseBtn = btnCode & ~32; // strip motion bit\n\n  let button: MouseEvent[\"button\"];\n  let type: MouseEvent[\"type\"];\n\n  if (baseBtn === 64) {\n    return { x, y, button: \"scrollUp\", type: \"press\" };\n  }\n  if (baseBtn === 65) {\n    return { x, y, button: \"scrollDown\", type: \"press\" };\n  }\n\n  switch (baseBtn & 3) {\n    case 0:\n      button = \"left\";\n      break;\n    case 1:\n      button = \"middle\";\n      break;\n    case 2:\n      button = \"right\";\n      break;\n    case 3:\n      button = \"none\";\n      break;\n    default:\n      button = \"none\";\n  }\n\n  if (isRelease) {\n    type = \"release\";\n  } else if (isMotion) {\n    type = \"move\";\n  } else {\n    type = \"press\";\n  }\n\n  return { x, y, button, type };\n}\n"
}

  "content": "import { useRef, useCallback } from \"react\";\nimport { useStdout } from \"ink\";\nimport { useMouse, type MouseEvent } from \"./useMouse.js\";\nimport { useStore } from \"../store/index.js\";\n\ntype DragTarget = \"left\" | \"right\" | null;\n\nconst EDGE_TOLERANCE = 1; // columns from border edge to trigger resize\n\n/**\n * Enables mouse-driven sidebar resizing.\n * Detects click on sidebar edges and drags to resize.\n */\nexport function useResizableSidebars(): void {\n  const { stdout } = useStdout();\n  const dragTarget = useRef<DragTarget>(null);\n  const dragStartX = useRef(0);\n  const dragStartWidth = useRef(0);\n\n  const handleMouse = useCallback(\n    (event: MouseEvent) => {\n      const termWidth = stdout?.columns ?? 120;\n      const leftWidth = useStore.getState().leftSidebarWidth;\n      const rightWidth = useStore.getState().rightSidebarWidth;\n      const setLeft = useStore.getState().setLeftSidebarWidth;\n      const setRight = useStore.getState().setRightSidebarWidth;\n\n      // Left sidebar right edge is at column leftWidth (0-based)\n      const leftEdge = leftWidth;\n      // Right sidebar left edge is at column (termWidth - rightWidth)\n      const rightEdge = termWidth - rightWidth;\n\n      if (event.type === \"press\" && event.button === \"left\") {\n        // Check if clicking on left sidebar edge\n        if (Math.abs(event.x - leftEdge) <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {\n          dragTarget.current = \"left\";\n          dragStartX.current = event.x;\n          dragStartWidth.current = leftWidth;\n          return;\n        }\n        // Check if clicking on right sidebar edge\n        if (Math.abs(event.x - rightEdge) <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {\n          dragTarget.current = \"right\";\n          dragStartX.current = event.x;\n          dragStartWidth.current = rightWidth;\n          return;\n        }\n      }\n\n      if (event.type === \"move\" && dragTarget.current) {\n        const deltaX = event.x - dragStartX.current;\n\n        if (dragTarget.current === \"left\") {\n          setLeft(dragStartWidth.current + deltaX);\n        } else if (dragTarget.current === \"right\") {\n          // Dragging left = increase width, dragging right = decrease\n          setRight(dragStartWidth.current - deltaX);\n        }\n        return;\n      }\n\n      if (event.type === \"release\") {\n        dragTarget.current = null;\n      }\n    },\n    [stdout]\n  );\n\n  useMouse(handleMouse);\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

The problem is that `stdin.on("data")` receives data, but Ink's internal input handler ALSO reads from stdin. We need to intercept stdin *before* Ink sees it and strip mouse sequences. The way to do this is to monkey-patch `stdin.emit` to filter out mouse data.

1	import { useRef, useCallback } from "react";
2	import { useStdout } from "ink";
3	import { useMouse, type MouseEvent } from "./useMouse.js";
4	import { useStore } from "../store/index.js";
5	
6	type DragTarget = "left" | "right" | null;
7	
8	const EDGE_TOLERANCE = 1; // columns from border edge to trigger resize
9	
10	/**
11	 * Enables mouse-driven sidebar resizing.
12	 * Detects click on sidebar edges and drags to resize.
13	 */
14	export function useResizableSidebars(): void {
15	  const { stdout } = useStdout();
16	  const dragTarget = useRef<DragTarget>(null);
17	  const dragStartX = useRef(0);
18	  const dragStartWidth = useRef(0);
19	
20	  const handleMouse = useCallback(
21	    (event: MouseEvent) => {
22	      const termWidth = stdout?.columns ?? 120;
23	      const leftWidth = useStore.getState().leftSidebarWidth;
24	      const rightWidth = useStore.getState().rightSidebarWidth;
25	      const setLeft = useStore.getState().setLeftSidebarWidth;
26	      const setRight = useStore.getState().setRightSidebarWidth;
27	
28	      // Left sidebar right edge is at column leftWidth (0-based)
29	      const leftEdge = leftWidth;
30	      // Right sidebar left edge is at column (termWidth - rightWidth)
31	      const rightEdge = termWidth - rightWidth;
32	
33	      if (event.type === "press" && event.button === "left") {
34	        // Check if clicking on left sidebar edge
35	        if (Math.abs(event.x - leftEdge) <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
36	          dragTarget.current = "left";
37	          dragStartX.current = event.x;
38	          dragStartWidth.current = leftWidth;
39	          return;
40	        }
41	        // Check if clicking on right sidebar edge
42	        if (Math.abs(event.x - rightEdge) <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
43	          dragTarget.current = "right";
44	          dragStartX.current = event.x;
45	          dragStartWidth.current = rightWidth;
46	          return;
47	        }
48	      }
49	
50	      if (event.type === "move" && dragTarget.current) {
51	        const deltaX = event.x - dragStartX.current;
52	
53	        if (dragTarget.current === "left") {
54	          setLeft(dragStartWidth.current + deltaX);
55	        } else if (dragTarget.current === "right") {
56	          // Dragging left = increase width, dragging right = decrease
57	          setRight(dragStartWidth.current - deltaX);
58	        }
59	        return;
60	      }
61	
62	      if (event.type === "release") {
63	        dragTarget.current = null;
64	      }
65	    },
66	    [stdout]
67	  );
68	
69	  useMouse(handleMouse);
70	}
71

The problem: Ink's `useStdin()` returns a wrapper, not `process.stdin`. Patching the wrapper's `emit` doesn't intercept the real stdin. Need to patch `process.stdin` directly.

120;\n      const leftWidth = useStore.getState().leftSidebarWidth;\n      const rightWidth = useStore.getState().rightSidebarWidth;\n      const setLeft = useStore.getState().setLeftSidebarWidth;\n      const setRight = useStore.getState().setRightSidebarWidth;\n\n      // Left sidebar right edge: border is at column (leftWidth - 1)\n      const leftEdge = leftWidth - 1;\n      // Right sidebar left edge: border is at column (termWidth - rightWidth)\n      const rightEdge = termWidth - rightWidth;\n\n      if (event.type === \"press\" && event.button === \"left\") {\n        if (Math.abs(event.x - leftEdge) <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {\n          dragTarget.current = \"left\";\n          dragStartX.current = event.x;\n          dragStartWidth.current = leftWidth;\n          return;\n        }\n        if (Math.abs(event.x - rightEdge) <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {\n          dragTarget.current = \"right\";\n          dragStartX.current = event.x;\n          dragStartWidth.current = rightWidth;\n          return;\n        }\n      }\n\n      if (event.type === \"move\" && dragTarget.current) {\n        const deltaX = event.x - dragStartX.current;\n\n        if (dragTarget.current === \"left\") {\n          setLeft(dragStartWidth.current + deltaX);\n        } else if (dragTarget.current === \"right\") {\n          setRight(dragStartWidth.current - deltaX);\n        }\n        return;\n      }\n\n      if (event.type === \"release\") {\n        dragTarget.current = null;\n      }\n    },\n    [stdout]\n  );\n\n  useMouse(handleMouse);\n}\n"

  "content": "import { useEffect, useRef } from \"react\";\n\nexport interface MouseEvent {\n  x: number; // 0-based column\n  y: number; // 0-based row\n  button: \"left\" | \"right\" | \"middle\" | \"none\" | \"scrollUp\" | \"scrollDown\";\n  type: \"press\" | \"release\" | \"move\";\n}\n\ntype MouseHandler = (event: MouseEvent) => void;\n\n// Matches SGR mouse sequences: \\x1b[<Btn;X;Y[Mm]\nconst SGR_MOUSE_RE = /\\x1b\\[<\\d+;\\d+;\\d+[Mm]/g;\nconst SGR_PARSE_RE = /\\x1b\\[<(\\d+);(\\d+);(\\d+)([Mm])/g;\n\n/**\n * Enables xterm SGR mouse tracking and emits parsed mouse events.\n * Patches process.stdin.read() to strip mouse sequences before Ink sees them,\n * since Ink 6 uses the readable stream interface (not data events).\n */\nexport function useMouse(onMouse: MouseHandler): void {\n  const handlerRef = useRef(onMouse);\n  handlerRef.current = onMouse;\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const stdin = process.stdin;\n\n    const enableSeq = \"\\x1b[?1000h\\x1b[?1002h\\x1b[?1006h\";\n    const disableSeq = \"\\x1b[?1006l\\x1b[?1002l\\x1b[?1000l\";\n\n    process.stdout.write(enableSeq);\n\n    // Patch stdin.read() — Ink calls this in its 'readable' handler\n    const originalRead = stdin.read.bind(stdin);\n\n    (stdin as any).read = function patchedRead(size?: number): Buffer | string | null {\n      const chunk = originalRead(size);\n      if (chunk === null) return null;\n\n      const str = typeof chunk === \"string\" ? chunk : chunk.toString(\"utf-8\");\n\n      // Fast path: no mouse sequences\n      if (!str.includes(\"\\x1b[<\")) {\n        return chunk;\n      }\n\n      // Parse and dispatch mouse events\n      const parseRegex = new RegExp(SGR_PARSE_RE.source, \"g\");\n      let match: RegExpExecArray | null;\n      while ((match = parseRegex.exec(str)) !== null) {\n        const btnCode = parseInt(match[1], 10);\n        const x = parseInt(match[2], 10) - 1;\n        const y = parseInt(match[3], 10) - 1;\n        const isRelease = match[4] === \"m\";\n        const mouseEvt = parseSgrButton(btnCode, x, y, isRelease);\n        if (mouseEvt) {\n          handlerRef.current(mouseEvt);\n        }\n      }\n\n      // Strip mouse sequences\n      const cleaned = str.replace(SGR_MOUSE_RE, \"\");\n      if (cleaned.length === 0) {\n        // All data was mouse — return null so Ink skips this chunk\n        return null;\n      }\n\n      return Buffer.from(cleaned, \"utf-8\");\n    };\n\n    return () => {\n      (stdin as any).read = originalRead;\n      process.stdout.write(disableSeq);\n    };\n  }, []);\n}\n\nfunction parseSgrButton(\n  btnCode: number,\n  x: number,\n  y: number,\n  isRelease: boolean\n): MouseEvent | null {\n  const isMotion = (btnCode & 32) !== 0;\n  const baseBtn = btnCode & ~32;\n\n  let button: MouseEvent[\"button\"];\n  let type: MouseEvent[\"type\"];\n\n  if (baseBtn === 64) {\n    return { x, y, button: \"scrollUp\", type: \"press\" };\n  }\n  if (baseBtn === 65) {\n    return { x, y, button: \"scrollDown\", type: \"press\" };\n  }\n\n  switch (baseBtn & 3) {\n    case 0:\n      button = \"left\";\n      break;\n    case 1:\n      button = \"middle\";\n      break;\n    case 2:\n      button = \"right\";\n      break;\n    case 3:\n      button = \"none\";\n      break;\n    default:\n      button = \"none\";\n  }\n\n  if (isRelease) {\n    type = \"release\";\n  } else if (isMotion) {\n    type = \"move\";\n  } else {\n    type = \"press\";\n  }\n\n  return { x, y, button, type };\n}\n"

  "content": "import { Transform, type TransformCallback } from \"node:stream\";\nimport { EventEmitter } from \"node:events\";\n\nexport interface MouseEvent {\n  x: number;\n  y: number;\n  button: \"left\" | \"right\" | \"middle\" | \"none\" | \"scrollUp\" | \"scrollDown\";\n  type: \"press\" | \"release\" | \"move\";\n}\n\nconst SGR_MOUSE_RE = /\\x1b\\[<\\d+;\\d+;\\d+[Mm]/g;\nconst SGR_PARSE_RE = /\\x1b\\[<(\\d+);(\\d+);(\\d+)([Mm])/g;\n\n/**\n * Global event bus for mouse events.\n * Components subscribe via mouseEvents.on('mouse', handler).\n */\nexport const mouseEvents = new EventEmitter();\n\n/**\n * Transform stream that strips SGR mouse sequences from stdin\n * and emits them as parsed events on the mouseEvents bus.\n * Pass this as stdin to Ink's render().\n */\nexport class MouseFilterStream extends Transform {\n  private partial = \"\";\n\n  constructor() {\n    super();\n  }\n\n  _transform(chunk: Buffer, _encoding: string, callback: TransformCallback): void {\n    const str = this.partial + chunk.toString(\"utf-8\");\n    this.partial = \"\";\n\n    // Check for potential partial escape sequence at end of string\n    const lastEsc = str.lastIndexOf(\"\\x1b\");\n    let processStr: string;\n    if (lastEsc >= 0 && lastEsc > str.length - 20) {\n      // Might be a partial mouse sequence — buffer it\n      const tail = str.slice(lastEsc);\n      if (!tail.match(/\\x1b\\[<\\d+;\\d+;\\d+[Mm]/)) {\n        // Incomplete — save for next chunk\n        this.partial = tail;\n        processStr = str.slice(0, lastEsc);\n      } else {\n        processStr = str;\n      }\n    } else {\n      processStr = str;\n    }\n\n    // Parse and emit mouse events\n    const parseRegex = new RegExp(SGR_PARSE_RE.source, \"g\");\n    let match: RegExpExecArray | null;\n    while ((match = parseRegex.exec(processStr)) !== null) {\n      const btnCode = parseInt(match[1], 10);\n      const x = parseInt(match[2], 10) - 1;\n      const y = parseInt(match[3], 10) - 1;\n      const isRelease = match[4] === \"m\";\n      const evt = parseSgrButton(btnCode, x, y, isRelease);\n      if (evt) {\n        mouseEvents.emit(\"mouse\", evt);\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Strip mouse sequences and forward clean data to Ink\n    const cleaned = processStr.replace(SGR_MOUSE_RE, \"\");\n    if (cleaned.length > 0) {\n      this.push(Buffer.from(cleaned, \"utf-8\"));\n    }\n\n    callback();\n  }\n\n  _flush(callback: TransformCallback): void {\n    if (this.partial.length > 0) {\n      this.push(Buffer.from(this.partial, \"utf-8\"));\n      this.partial = \"\";\n    }\n    callback();\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Enable xterm SGR mouse tracking.\n * Call once at startup, before Ink renders.\n */\nexport function enableMouseTracking(): void {\n  process.stdout.write(\"\\x1b[?1000h\\x1b[?1002h\\x1b[?1006h\");\n}\n\n/**\n * Disable mouse tracking. Call on exit.\n */\nexport function disableMouseTracking(): void {\n  process.stdout.write(\"\\x1b[?1006l\\x1b[?1002l\\x1b[?1000l\");\n}\n\nfunction parseSgrButton(\n  btnCode: number,\n  x: number,\n  y: number,\n  isRelease: boolean\n): MouseEvent | null {\n  const isMotion = (btnCode & 32) !== 0;\n  const baseBtn = btnCode & ~32;\n\n  let button: MouseEvent[\"button\"];\n  let type: MouseEvent[\"type\"];\n\n  if (baseBtn === 64) return { x, y, button: \"scrollUp\", type: \"press\" };\n  if (baseBtn === 65) return { x, y, button: \"scrollDown\", type: \"press\" };\n\n  switch (baseBtn & 3) {\n    case 0: button = \"left\"; break;\n    case 1: button = \"middle\"; break;\n    case 2: button = \"right\"; break;\n    default: button = \"none\";\n  }\n\n  if (isRelease) type = \"release\";\n  else if (isMotion) type = \"move\";\n  else type = \"press\";\n\n  return { x, y, button, type };\n}\n"
}

> AGENT

Clean build. Completely different architecture now:

1. **`MouseFilterStream`** — Transform stream piped between `process.stdin` and Ink. Strips all SGR mouse sequences *before* Ink ever reads them. Emits parsed events on a global EventEmitter.
2. **`useMouse` hook** — just subscribes to the event bus. No stdin patching.
3. **`index.tsx`** — pipes `process.stdin → MouseFilterStream → Ink`, with TTY properties forwarded so Ink works normally.

Mouse sequences physically cannot reach Ink's input handling now. Try it.

1	import { Transform, type TransformCallback } from "node:stream";
2	import { EventEmitter } from "node:events";
3	
4	export interface MouseEvent {
5	  x: number;
6	  y: number;
7	  button: "left" | "right" | "middle" | "none" | "scrollUp" | "scrollDown";
8	  type: "press" | "release" | "move";
9	}
10	
11	const SGR_MOUSE_RE = /\x1b\[<\d+;\d+;\d+[Mm]/g;
12	const SGR_PARSE_RE = /\x1b\[<(\d+);(\d+);(\d+)([Mm])/g;
13	
14	/**
15	 * Global event bus for mouse events.
16	 * Components subscribe via mouseEvents.on('mouse', handler).
17	 */
18	export const mouseEvents = new EventEmitter();
19	
20	/**
21	 * Transform stream that strips SGR mouse sequences from stdin
22	 * and emits them as parsed events on the mouseEvents bus.
23	 * Pass this as stdin to Ink's render().
24	 */
25	export class MouseFilterStream extends Transform {
26	  private partial = "";
27	
28	  constructor() {
29	    super();
30	  }
31	
32	  _transform(chunk: Buffer, _encoding: string, callback: TransformCallback): void {
33	    const str = this.partial + chunk.toString("utf-8");
34	    this.partial = "";
35	
36	    // Check for potential partial escape sequence at end of string
37	    const lastEsc = str.lastIndexOf("\x1b");
38	    let processStr: string;
39	    if (lastEsc >= 0 && lastEsc > str.length - 20) {
40	      // Might be a partial mouse sequence — buffer it
41	      const tail = str.slice(lastEsc);
42	      if (!tail.match(/\x1b\[<\d+;\d+;\d+[Mm]/)) {
43	        // Incomplete — save for next chunk
44	        this.partial = tail;
45	        processStr = str.slice(0, lastEsc);
46	      } else {
47	        processStr = str;
48	      }
49	    } else {
50	      processStr = str;
51	    }
52	
53	    // Parse and emit mouse events
54	    const parseRegex = new RegExp(SGR_PARSE_RE.source, "g");
55	    let match: RegExpExecArray | null;
56	    while ((match = parseRegex.exec(processStr)) !== null) {
57	      const btnCode = parseInt(match[1], 10);
58	      const x = parseInt(match[2], 10) - 1;
59	      const y = parseInt(match[3], 10) - 1;
60	      const isRelease = match[4] === "m";
61	      const evt = parseSgrButton(btnCode, x, y, isRelease);
62	      if (evt) {
63	        mouseEvents.emit("mouse", evt);
64	      }
65	    }
66	
67	    // Strip mouse sequences and forward clean data to Ink
68	    const cleaned = processStr.replace(SGR_MOUSE_RE, "");
69	    if (cleaned.length > 0) {
70	      this.push(Buffer.from(cleaned, "utf-8"));
71	    }
72	
73	    callback();
74	  }
75	
76	  _flush(callback: TransformCallback): void {
77	    if (this.partial.length > 0) {
78	      this.push(Buffer.from(this.partial, "utf-8"));
79	      this.partial = "";
80	    }
81	    callback();
82	  }
83	}
84	
85	/**
86	 * Enable xterm SGR mouse tracking.
87	 * Call once at startup, before Ink renders.
88	 */
89	export function enableMouseTracking(): void {
90	  process.stdout.write("\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1002h\x1b[?1006h");
91	}
92	
93	/**
94	 * Disable mouse tracking. Call on exit.
95	 */
96	export function disableMouseTracking(): void {
97	  process.stdout.write("\x1b[?1006l\x1b[?1002l\x1b[?1000l");
98	}
99	
100	function parseSgrButton(
101	  btnCode: number,
102	  x: number,
103	  y: number,
104	  isRelease: boolean
105	): MouseEvent | null {
106	  const isMotion = (btnCode & 32) !== 0;
107	  const baseBtn = btnCode & ~32;
108	
109	  let button: MouseEvent["button"];
110	  let type: MouseEvent["type"];
111	
112	  if (baseBtn === 64) return { x, y, button: "scrollUp", type: "press" };
113	  if (baseBtn === 65) return { x, y, button: "scrollDown", type: "press" };
114	
115	  switch (baseBtn & 3) {
116	    case 0: button = "left"; break;
117	    case 1: button = "middle"; break;
118	    case 2: button = "right"; break;
119	    default: button = "none";
120	  }
121	
122	  if (isRelease) type = "release";
123	  else if (isMotion) type = "move";
124	  else type = "press";
125	
126	  return { x, y, button, type };
127	}
128

29	  const lineWidth = Math.max(10, termWidth - leftW - rightW - 6);
30	  function handleSubmit(): void {
31	    const trimmed = value.trim();

45	    });
46	  }, [disabled, cursorOffset]);

66	        setCursorOffset(cursorOffset - 1);

68	      return;
69	    }
70	    if (key.leftArrow) {
71	      setCursorOffset(Math.max(0, cursorOffset - 1));
72	      return;
73	    }
74	    if (key.rightArrow) {
75	      setCursorOffset(Math.min(value.length, cursorOffset + 1));
76	      return;
77	    }
78	    if (key.upArrow) {
79	      // Move cursor up one line width
80	      setCursorOffset(Math.max(0, cursorOffset - lineWidth));
81	      return;
82	    }

110	  // Wrap text into visual lines (handle both soft wrap and \n)
111	  function wrapText(text: string, width: number): string[] {
112	    const result: string[] = [];
113	    const hardLines = text.split("\n");
114	    for (const hardLine of hardLines) {
115	      if (hardLine.length === 0) {
116	        result.push("");
117	      } else {
118	        for (let i = 0; i < hardLine.length; i += width) {
119	          result.push(hardLine.slice(i, i + width));
120	        }
121	      }
122	    }
123	    if (result.length === 0) result.push("");
124	    return result;
125	  }

127	  // Find which visual line the cursor is on
128	  function getCursorVisualPos(text: string, cursor: number, width: number): { line: number; col: number } {
129	    let line = 0;
130	    let remaining = cursor;
131	    const hardLines = text.split("\n");
132	
133	    for (let h = 0; h < hardLines.length; h++) {
134	      const hLen = hardLines[h].length;
135	      if (remaining <= hLen) {
136	        // Cursor is in this hard line
137	        line += Math.floor(remaining / width);
138	        return { line, col: remaining % width };
139	      }
140	      // Account for soft-wrapped lines of this hard line
141	      line += Math.max(1, Math.ceil(hLen / width));
142	      remaining -= hLen + 1; // +1 for the \n
143	    }
144	    return { line, col: 0 };
145	  }

215	          const isCursorLine = idx === cursorVisLine;

1	import { Transform, type TransformCallback } from "node:stream";
2	import { EventEmitter } from "node:events";
3	
4	export interface MouseEvent {
5	  x: number;
6	  y: number;
7	  button: "left" | "right" | "middle" | "none" | "scrollUp" | "scrollDown";
8	  type: "press" | "release" | "move";
9	}
10	
11	const SGR_MOUSE_RE = /\x1b\[<\d+;\d+;\d+[Mm]/g;
12	const SGR_PARSE_RE = /\x1b\[<(\d+);(\d+);(\d+)([Mm])/g;
13	
14	// CSI sequences for modified keys that Ink doesn't understand.
15	// Shift+Enter: \x1b[27;2;13~   Ctrl+Enter: \x1b[27;5;13~
16	const MODIFIED_KEY_RE = /\x1b\[27;\d+;\d+~/g;
17	
18	
19	/**
20	 * Global event bus for mouse events.
21	 * Components subscribe via mouseEvents.on('mouse', handler).
22	 */
23	export const mouseEvents = new EventEmitter();
24	
25	/**
26	 * Transform stream that strips SGR mouse sequences from stdin
27	 * and emits them as parsed events on the mouseEvents bus.
28	 * Pass this as stdin to Ink's render().
29	 */
30	export class MouseFilterStream extends Transform {
31	  private partial = "";
32	
33	  constructor() {
34	    super();
35	  }
36	
37	  _transform(chunk: Buffer, _encoding: string, callback: TransformCallback): void {
38	    const str = this.partial + chunk.toString("utf-8");
39	    this.partial = "";
40	
41	    // Only buffer partial sequences that could be incomplete MOUSE sequences.
42	    // Mouse sequences start with \x1b[< — only buffer tails matching that prefix.
43	    let processStr = str;
44	    const lastEsc = str.lastIndexOf("\x1b");
45	    if (lastEsc >= 0 && lastEsc > str.length - 20) {
46	      const tail = str.slice(lastEsc);
47	      // Only buffer if it looks like the start of a mouse sequence (\x1b, \x1b[, \x1b[<, \x1b[<digits...)
48	      // but is NOT yet complete
49	      if (/^\x1b(\[(<(\d+(;\d+(;\d+[Mm]?)?)?)?)?)?$/.test(tail) && !tail.match(/\x1b\[<\d+;\d+;\d+[Mm]/)) {
50	        this.partial = tail;
51	        processStr = str.slice(0, lastEsc);
52	      }
53	    }
54	
55	    // Parse and emit mouse events
56	    const parseRegex = new RegExp(SGR_PARSE_RE.source, "g");
57	    let match: RegExpExecArray | null;
58	    while ((match = parseRegex.exec(processStr)) !== null) {
59	      const btnCode = parseInt(match[1], 10);
60	      const x = parseInt(match[2], 10) - 1;
61	      const y = parseInt(match[3], 10) - 1;
62	      const isRelease = match[4] === "m";
63	      const evt = parseSgrButton(btnCode, x, y, isRelease);
64	      if (evt) {
65	        mouseEvents.emit("mouse", evt);
66	      }
67	    }
68	
69	    // Emit shift+enter as a custom event
70	    if (processStr.includes("\x1b[27;2;13~")) {
71	      mouseEvents.emit("shift-enter");
72	    }
73	
74	    // Strip mouse sequences and modified key sequences, forward clean data to Ink
75	    const cleaned = processStr
76	      .replace(SGR_MOUSE_RE, "")
77	      .replace(MODIFIED_KEY_RE, "");
78	    if (cleaned.length > 0) {
79	      this.push(Buffer.from(cleaned, "utf-8"));
80	    }
81	
82	    callback();
83	  }
84	
85	  _flush(callback: TransformCallback): void {
86	    if (this.partial.length > 0) {
87	      this.push(Buffer.from(this.partial, "utf-8"));
88	      this.partial = "";
89	    }
90	    callback();
91	  }
92	}
93	
94	/**
95	 * Enable xterm SGR mouse tracking.
96	 * Call once at startup, before Ink renders.
97	 */
98	export function enableMouseTracking(): void {
99	  process.stdout.write("\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1002h\x1b[?1006h");
100	}
101	
102	/**
103	 * Disable mouse tracking. Call on exit.
104	 */
105	export function disableMouseTracking(): void {
106	  process.stdout.write("\x1b[?1006l\x1b[?1002l\x1b[?1000l");
107	}
108	
109	function parseSgrButton(
110	  btnCode: number,
111	  x: number,
112	  y: number,
113	  isRelease: boolean
114	): MouseEvent | null {
115	  const isMotion = (btnCode & 32) !== 0;
116	  const baseBtn = btnCode & ~32;
117	
118	  let button: MouseEvent["button"];
119	  let type: MouseEvent["type"];
120	
121	  if (baseBtn === 64) return { x, y, button: "scrollUp", type: "press" };
122	  if (baseBtn === 65) return { x, y, button: "scrollDown", type: "press" };
123	
124	  switch (baseBtn & 3) {
125	    case 0: button = "left"; break;
126	    case 1: button = "middle"; break;
127	    case 2: button = "right"; break;
128	    default: button = "none";
129	  }
130	
131	  if (isRelease) type = "release";
132	  else if (isMotion) type = "move";
133	  else type = "press";
134	
135	  return { x, y, button, type };
136	}
137

  "new_string": "    // Emit shift+enter\n    if (processStr.includes(\"\\x1b[27;2;13~\")) {\n      mouseEvents.emit(\"shift-enter\");\n    }\n\n    // Emit modified arrow keys (shift+arrows)\n    const arrowRegex = new RegExp(MODIFIED_ARROW_RE.source, \"g\");\n    let arrowMatch: RegExpExecArray | null;\n    while ((arrowMatch = arrowRegex.exec(processStr)) !== null) {\n      const modifier = parseInt(arrowMatch[1], 10);\n      const direction = arrowMatch[2];\n      // modifier 2 = shift\n      if (modifier === 2) {\n        if (direction === \"D\") mouseEvents.emit(\"shift-left\");\n        if (direction === \"C\") mouseEvents.emit(\"shift-right\");\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Emit alt+backspace (\\x1b + \\x7f)\n    if (processStr.includes(\"\\x1b\\x7f\")) {\n      mouseEvents.emit(\"alt-backspace\");\n    }\n\n    // Emit alt+delete\n    if (processStr.includes(\"\\x1b[3;3~\")) {\n      mouseEvents.emit(\"alt-delete\");\n    }\n\n    // Strip all special sequences, forward clean data to Ink\n    const cleaned = processStr\n      .replace(SGR_MOUSE_RE, \"\")\n      .replace(MODIFIED_KEY_RE, \"\")\n      .replace(MODIFIED_ARROW_RE, \"\")\n      .replace(ALT_DELETE_RE, \"\")\n      .replace(/\\x1b\\x7f/g, \"\");\n    if (cleaned.length > 0) {\n      this.push(Buffer.from(cleaned, \"utf-8\"));\n    }"

> AGENT

Clean build. Here's what's implemented:

**Alt/Option+Backspace** — deletes word left (skips whitespace, then word chars)
**Alt/Option+Delete** — deletes word right
**Shift+Left/Right** — extends selection character by character, highlighted in blue
**Typing/backspace with selection** — replaces/deletes the selected text
**Regular arrows** — clear selection and move cursor

All special key sequences are intercepted in MouseFilterStream and emitted as events, so they never leak as text into the UI.

Updated requirement: Shift+Alt+Arrows = select by words, Shift+Cmd+Arrows = select by lines.

CSI modifier codes: `\x1b[1;NX` where N = modifier, X = direction:
- N=2: Shift
- N=4: Shift+Alt (2+2... actually 3=Alt, 4=Shift+Alt)
- N=10: Shift+Cmd (on macOS, 9=Cmd, 10=Shift+Cmd)

> AGENT

The issue is in the width clamping. When one sidebar gets wide, the max for the other becomes very small. Then when you try to resize, the clamp prevents it because `maxRight = termWidth - leftW - minCenter` is already near the limit.

The real bug: `setLeftSidebarWidth` reads `rightSidebarWidth` from state at call time, but during a drag the values are stale because `dragStartWidth` is captured at press time.

1	import { useRef, useCallback } from "react";
2	import { useStdout } from "ink";
3	import { useMouse, type MouseEvent } from "./useMouse.js";
4	import { useStore } from "../store/index.js";
5	
6	type DragTarget = "left" | "right" | null;
7	
8	const EDGE_TOLERANCE = 2; // columns from border edge to trigger resize
9	
10	/**
11	 * Enables mouse-driven sidebar resizing.
12	 * Detects click on sidebar edges and drags to resize.
13	 */
14	export function useResizableSidebars(): void {
15	  const { stdout } = useStdout();
16	  const dragTarget = useRef<DragTarget>(null);
17	  const dragStartX = useRef(0);
18	  const dragStartWidth = useRef(0);
19	
20	  const handleMouse = useCallback(
21	    (event: MouseEvent) => {
22	      const termWidth = stdout?.columns ?? 120;
23	      const leftWidth = useStore.getState().leftSidebarWidth;
24	      const rightWidth = useStore.getState().rightSidebarWidth;
25	      const setLeft = useStore.getState().setLeftSidebarWidth;
26	      const setRight = useStore.getState().setRightSidebarWidth;
27	
28	      // Left sidebar right edge: border is at column (leftWidth - 1)
29	      const leftEdge = leftWidth - 1;
30	      // Right sidebar left edge: border is at column (termWidth - rightWidth)
31	      const rightEdge = termWidth - rightWidth;
32	
33	      if (event.type === "press" && event.button === "left") {
34	        if (Math.abs(event.x - leftEdge) <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
35	          dragTarget.current = "left";
36	          dragStartX.current = event.x;
37	          dragStartWidth.current = leftWidth;
38	          return;
39	        }
40	        if (Math.abs(event.x - rightEdge) <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
41	          dragTarget.current = "right";
42	          dragStartX.current = event.x;
43	          dragStartWidth.current = rightWidth;
44	          return;
45	        }
46	      }
47	
48	      if (event.type === "move" && dragTarget.current) {
49	        const deltaX = event.x - dragStartX.current;
50	
51	        if (dragTarget.current === "left") {
52	          setLeft(dragStartWidth.current + deltaX);
53	        } else if (dragTarget.current === "right") {
54	          setRight(dragStartWidth.current - deltaX);
55	        }
56	        return;
57	      }
58	
59	      if (event.type === "release") {
60	        dragTarget.current = null;
61	      }
62	    },
63	    [stdout]
64	  );
65	
66	  useMouse(handleMouse);
67	}
68

> AGENT

The problem: edge detection uses current widths from store, but after resizing the left sidebar wide, the right sidebar's edge position shifts. The edge detection then fails because the coordinates don't match anymore. Also the drag uses `dragStartWidth + delta` which doesn't account for the shifted positions.

Simpler approach: during drag, just set width directly from mouse X position instead of using deltas.

> AGENT

Fixed. Changed from delta-based to position-based resize:

- **Left sidebar**: width = mouse X position directly
- **Right sidebar**: width = terminal width - mouse X position
- Both clamped live against current opposite sidebar width, so they can never overlap
- No more stale `dragStartWidth` — reads fresh state each move event

ok it stacked when i resize both side bar in a way, then middle pane has the smalest size

> AGENT

The left sidebar lost its border and content — it's been resized so wide it pushed everything off. The edge detection then can't find the border anymore, so dragging stops working.

The issue: when left sidebar gets very wide, its right edge moves past where the right sidebar edge detection starts. The two edges overlap and it gets stuck.

Fix: also clamp in the store setters to use fresh opposite width, and increase `MIN_CENTER` so the middle pane never gets this small.

> AGENT

Two fixes:

1. **Closest edge wins** — when both edges are within tolerance (sidebars close together), picks the nearest one instead of always matching left first
2. **Reset on every press** — clears any stuck drag before starting new edge detection, so missed release events can't permanently break things

> AGENT

Terminals don't support custom mouse pointer shapes (resize cursor etc.) — that's a GUI-only feature.

**What we can do:** change the border color when hovering near the edge. Visual feedback that it's draggable.

import React from "react";
import { Box, useStdout } from "ink";
import { FeatureBar } from "./FeatureBar.js";
import { useStore } from "../store/index.js";
import { useResizableSidebars } from "../hooks/useResizableSidebars.js";

interface LayoutProps {
  sessionSidebar: React.ReactNode;
  center: React.ReactNode;
  skillsSidebar: React.ReactNode;
}

export function Layout({
  sessionSidebar,
  center,
  skillsSidebar,
}: LayoutProps): React.ReactElement {
  const { stdout } = useStdout();
  const termHeight = stdout?.rows ?? 40;
  const leftWidth = useStore((s) => s.leftSidebarWidth);
  const rightWidth = useStore((s) => s.rightSidebarWidth);

  useResizableSidebars();

  return (
    <Box flexDirection="column" width="100%" height={termHeight}>
      <FeatureBar />

      <Box flexDirection="row" flexGrow={1}>
        <Box
          width={leftWidth}
          flexDirection="column"
          borderStyle="round"
          borderColor="gray"
        >
          {sessionSidebar}
        </Box>

        <Box flexDirection="column" flexGrow={1}>
          {center}
        </Box>

        <Box
          width={rightWidth}
          flexDirection="column"
          borderStyle="round"
          borderColor="gray"
        >
          {skillsSidebar}
        </Box>
      </Box>
    </Box>
  );
}
```

6	type DragTarget = "left" | "right" | null;
7	
8	const EDGE_TOLERANCE = 2;
9	const MIN_SIDEBAR = 10;
10	const MIN_CENTER = 40;
11	
12	export function useResizableSidebars(): void {
13	  const { stdout } = useStdout();
14	  const dragTarget = useRef<DragTarget>(null);
15	
16	  const handleMouse = useCallback(
17	    (event: MouseEvent) => {
18	      const termWidth = stdout?.columns ?? 120;
19	      const leftWidth = useStore.getState().leftSidebarWidth;
20	      const rightWidth = useStore.getState().rightSidebarWidth;
21	      const setLeft = useStore.getState().setLeftSidebarWidth;
22	      const setRight = useStore.getState().setRightSidebarWidth;
23	      const setHover = useStore.getState().setSidebarHover;
24	      const setDragging = useStore.getState().setSidebarDragging;
25	
26	      const leftEdge = leftWidth - 1;
27	      const rightEdge = termWidth - rightWidth;
28	
29	      const distLeft = Math.abs(event.x - leftEdge);
30	      const distRight = Math.abs(event.x - rightEdge);
31	
32	      // Update hover state on any move (even without drag)
33	      if (event.type === "move" && !dragTarget.current) {
34	        let hover: "left" | "right" | null = null;
35	        if (distLeft <= EDGE_TOLERANCE && distRight <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
36	          hover = distLeft <= distRight ? "left" : "right";
37	        } else if (distLeft <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
38	          hover = "left";
39	        } else if (distRight <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
40	          hover = "right";
41	        }
42	        if (hover !== useStore.getState().sidebarHover) {
43	          setHover(hover);
44	        }
45	      }
46	
47	      if (event.type === "press" && event.button === "left") {
48	        dragTarget.current = null;
49	
50	        if (distLeft <= EDGE_TOLERANCE && distRight <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
51	          dragTarget.current = distLeft <= distRight ? "left" : "right";
52	        } else if (distLeft <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
53	          dragTarget.current = "left";
54	        } else if (distRight <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
55	          dragTarget.current = "right";
56	        }
57	
58	        setDragging(dragTarget.current);
59	        return;
60	      }
61	
62	      if (event.type === "move" && dragTarget.current) {
63	        if (dragTarget.current === "left") {
64	          const maxLeft = termWidth - rightWidth - MIN_CENTER;
65	          setLeft(Math.max(MIN_SIDEBAR, Math.min(event.x + 1, maxLeft)));
66	        } else if (dragTarget.current === "right") {
67	          const maxRight = termWidth - leftWidth - MIN_CENTER;
68	          setRight(Math.max(MIN_SIDEBAR, Math.min(termWidth - event.x, maxRight)));
69	        }
70	        return;
71	      }
72	
73	      if (event.type === "release") {
74	        dragTarget.current = null;
75	        setDragging(null);
76	      }
77	    },
78	    [stdout]
79	  );
80	
81	  useMouse(handleMouse);
82	}
83

2	import { useStdout } from "ink";
3	import { useMouse, type MouseEvent } from "./useMouse.js";
4	import { useStore } from "../store/index.js";
5	
6	type DragTarget = "left" | "right" | null;
7	
8	const EDGE_TOLERANCE = 1;
9	const MIN_SIDEBAR = 10;
10	const MIN_CENTER = 40;
11	
12	export function useResizableSidebars(): void {
13	  const { stdout } = useStdout();
14	  const dragTarget = useRef<DragTarget>(null);
15	
16	  const handleMouse = useCallback(
17	    (event: MouseEvent) => {
18	      const termWidth = stdout?.columns ?? 120;
19	      const leftWidth = useStore.getState().leftSidebarWidth;
20	      const rightWidth = useStore.getState().rightSidebarWidth;
21	      const setLeft = useStore.getState().setLeftSidebarWidth;
22	      const setRight = useStore.getState().setRightSidebarWidth;
23	      const setHover = useStore.getState().setSidebarHover;
24	      const setDragging = useStore.getState().setSidebarDragging;
25	      useStore.getState().setDebugMouseX(event.x);
26	
27	      // Left sidebar: columns 0..leftWidth-1, right border at leftWidth-1
28	      // Right sidebar: columns termWidth-rightWidth..termWidth-1, left border at termWidth-rightWidth
29	      // The border character of left sidebar is the last column of its width
30	      // Try both: the exact border column AND its neighbor
31	      const leftEdge = leftWidth;
32	      const rightEdge = termWidth - rightWidth;
33	
34	      const distLeft = Math.abs(event.x - leftEdge);
35	      const distRight = Math.abs(event.x - rightEdge);
36	
37	      // Update hover state on any move (even without drag)
38	      if (event.type === "move" && !dragTarget.current) {
39	        let hover: "left" | "right" | null = null;
40	        if (distLeft <= EDGE_TOLERANCE && distRight <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
41	          hover = distLeft <= distRight ? "left" : "right";
42	        } else if (distLeft <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
43	          hover = "left";
44	        } else if (distRight <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
45	          hover = "right";
46	        }
47	        if (hover !== useStore.getState().sidebarHover) {
48	          setHover(hover);
49	        }
50	      }
51	
52	      if (event.type === "press" && event.button === "left") {
53	        dragTarget.current = null;
54	
55	        if (distLeft <= EDGE_TOLERANCE && distRight <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
56	          dragTarget.current = distLeft <= distRight ? "left" : "right";
57	        } else if (distLeft <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
58	          dragTarget.current = "left";
59	        } else if (distRight <= EDGE_TOLERANCE) {
60	          dragTarget.current = "right";
61	        }
62	
63	        setDragging(dragTarget.current);
64	        return;
65	      }
66	
67	      if (event.type === "move" && dragTarget.current) {
68	        if (dragTarget.current === "left") {
69	          const maxLeft = termWidth - rightWidth - MIN_CENTER;
70	          setLeft(Math.max(MIN_SIDEBAR, Math.min(event.x + 1, maxLeft)));
71	        } else if (dragTarget.current === "right") {
72	          const maxRight = termWidth - leftWidth - MIN_CENTER;
73	          setRight(Math.max(MIN_SIDEBAR, Math.min(termWidth - event.x, maxRight)));
74	        }
75	        return;
76	      }
77	
78	      if (event.type === "release") {
79	        dragTarget.current = null;
80	        setDragging(null);
81	      }
82	    },
83	    [stdout]
84	  );
85	
86	  useMouse(handleMouse);
87	}

Key change: on press, the drag target is set from **either** the edge detection **or** the current hover state — whichever matches. So if the border is highlighted yellow (hover active), clicking anywhere will grab it, even if the click coordinates are slightly off from the edge. The hover state acts as a "pre-grab" lock.

Done. Mouse text selection in the input:

- **Click** in the input area — places cursor at that position
- **Click + drag** — selects text from click point to drag point (highlighted in white/black)
- **Release** — if no movement, just places cursor (clears selection)

The coordinate mapping converts screen X/Y → visual line/column → absolute text offset, accounting for sidebar widths, borders, padding, prompt, and scroll position.

  "content": "import React from \"react\";\nimport { Box, Text, useInput } from \"ink\";\nimport { useStore } from \"../store/index.js\";\n\n/**\n * Top bar — full width, holds session tabs.\n */\nexport function FeatureBar(): React.ReactElement {\n  const tabs = useStore((s) => s.tabs);\n  const activeTabId = useStore((s) => s.activeTabId);\n  const setActiveTab = useStore((s) => s.setActiveTab);\n  const createTab = useStore((s) => s.createTab);\n  const closeTab = useStore((s) => s.closeTab);\n\n  useInput((input, key) => {\n    if (input === \"t\" && key.ctrl) {\n      createTab();\n      return;\n    }\n    if (input === \"w\" && key.ctrl && activeTabId) {\n      closeTab(activeTabId);\n      return;\n    }\n    if (key.ctrl && input >= \"1\" && input <= \"9\") {\n      const idx = parseInt(input, 10) - 1;\n      if (tabs[idx]) {\n        setActiveTab(tabs[idx].id);\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n    if (key.tab && !key.shift && tabs.length > 1) {\n      const currentIdx = tabs.findIndex((t) => t.id === activeTabId);\n      const nextIdx = (currentIdx + 1) % tabs.length;\n      setActiveTab(tabs[nextIdx].id);\n    }\n  });\n\n  return (\n    <Box\n      flexDirection=\"row\"\n      borderStyle=\"round\"\n      borderColor=\"gray\"\n      paddingX={1}\n      flexShrink={0}\n      height={3}\n    >\n      {tabs.map((tab) => (\n        <Box key={tab.id} paddingX={1}>\n          <Text\n            color={tab.id === activeTabId ? \"cyan\" : \"gray\"}\n            bold={tab.id === activeTabId}\n          >\n            {tab.index}: {tab.name}\n          </Text>\n        </Box>\n      ))}\n      <Box paddingX={1}>\n        <Text color=\"green\">[+]</Text>\n      </Box>\n    </Box>\n  );\n}\n"
}

(\n        <>\n          {data.model && <Text color=\"green\">{data.model}</Text>}\n          {data.model && <Text color=\"gray\">|</Text>}\n          <Text color=\"yellow\">Ctx: {formatTokens(data.contextTokens)}</Text>\n          <Text color=\"gray\">|</Text>\n          <Text color={data.contextPercent > 80 ? \"red\" : data.contextPercent > 50 ? \"yellow\" : \"green\"}>\n            {data.contextPercent.toFixed(0)}%\n          </Text>\n          <Text color=\"gray\">|</Text>\n          <Text color=\"cyan\">${data.cost.toFixed(2)}</Text>\n          {data.gitBranch && (\n            <>\n              <Text color=\"gray\">|</Text>\n              <Text color=\"yellow\">@ {data.gitBranch}</Text>\n            </>\n          )}\n          {data.gitDiffStats && (\n            <>\n              <Text color=\"gray\">|</Text>\n              <Text color=\"green\">+{data.gitDiffStats.added}</Text>\n              <Text color=\"red\"> -{data.gitDiffStats.removed}</Text>\n              <Text color=\"yellow\"> ~{data.gitDiffStats.modified}</Text>\n            </>\n          )}\n        </>\n      ) : (\n        <Text color=\"gray\">No active session</Text>\n      )}\n    </Box>\n  );\n}\n"
}

}

  "content": "import React, { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from \"react\";\nimport { Box, Text, useInput } from \"ink\";\nimport { SessionSidebar } from \"./SessionSidebar.js\";\nimport { GitPanel } from \"./GitPanel.js\";\nimport { FilesPanel } from \"./FilesPanel.js\";\nimport { mouseEvents, type MouseEvent } from \"../mouseStream.js\";\nimport { useStore } from \"../store/index.js\";\nimport type { Session } from \"../../shared/types.js\";\n\ntype LeftTab = \"sessions\" | \"git\" | \"files\";\n\nconst TABS: { key: LeftTab; label: string }[] = [\n  { key: \"sessions\", label: \" Sessions \" },\n  { key: \"git\", label: \" Git \" },\n  { key: \"files\", label: \" Files \" },\n];\n\ninterface LeftSidebarProps {\n  onOpenSession: (session: Session) => void;\n  visible: boolean;\n}\n\nexport function LeftSidebar({\n  onOpenSession,\n  visible,\n}: LeftSidebarProps): React.ReactElement {\n  const [activeTab, setActiveTab] = useState<LeftTab>(\"sessions\");\n  const leftW = useStore((s) => s.leftSidebarWidth);\n\n  useInput(\n    (input, key) => {\n      if (!visible) return;\n      if (key.meta && input === \"1\") { setActiveTab(\"sessions\"); return; }\n      if (key.meta && input === \"2\") { setActiveTab(\"git\"); return; }\n      if (key.meta && input === \"3\") { setActiveTab(\"files\"); return; }\n    },\n    { isActive: visible }\n  );\n\n  // Mouse click on tab buttons\n  // Tabs are in the first 3 rows (border + content + border) of the sidebar\n  // Each tab box has border (2) + label length, rendered in a row starting at x=1 (sidebar padding)\n  const handleMouse = useCallback(\n    (event: MouseEvent) => {\n      if (!visible) return;\n      if (event.type !== \"press\" || event.button !== \"left\") return;\n\n      // Tab row is at Y ~= 1 (inside the sidebar border, after the top feature bar which is 3 rows)\n      // The sidebar starts at X=0, tab content is inside border+padding\n      // FeatureBar takes 3 rows at top, sidebar border adds 1 row\n      const tabRowY = 4; // featureBar(3) + sidebar top border(1)\n\n      if (event.y !== tabRowY) return;\n      if (event.x >= leftW) return; // outside sidebar\n\n      // Calculate which tab was clicked based on X position\n      // Tabs are rendered as bordered boxes in a row, starting at x=1 (sidebar border)\n      // Each tab: border(1) + padding(1) + label + padding(1) + border(1) + gap\n      let xPos = 2; // sidebar border(1) + box start\n      for (const tab of TABS) {\n        const tabWidth = tab.label.length + 2; // border chars\n        if (event.x >= xPos && event.x < xPos + tabWidth) {\n          setActiveTab(tab.key);\n          return;\n        }\n        xPos += tabWidth;\n      }\n    },\n    [visible, leftW]\n  );\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    mouseEvents.on(\"mouse\", handleMouse);\n    return () => { mouseEvents.off(\"mouse\", handleMouse); };\n  }, [handleMouse]);\n\n  if (!visible) return <></>;\n\n  return (\n    <Box flexDirection=\"column\" flexGrow={1}>\n      {/* Tab buttons with borders */}\n      <Box flexDirection=\"row\">\n        {TABS.map((tab) => {\n          const isActive = activeTab === tab.key;\n          return (\n            <Box\n              key={tab.key}\n              borderStyle={isActive ? \"round\" : \"single\"}\n              borderColor={isActive ? \"cyan\" : \"gray\"}\n              borderBottom={false}\n            >\n              <Text\n                color={isActive ? \"cyan\" : \"gray\"}\n                bold={isActive}\n              >\n                {tab.label}\n              </Text>\n            </Box>\n          );\n        })}\n      </Box>\n\n      {/* Panel content */}\n      <Box flexDirection=\"column\" flexGrow={1}>\n        {activeTab === \"sessions\" && (\n          <SessionSidebar onOpenSession={onOpenSession} visible={visible} />\n        )}\n        {activeTab === \"git\" && <GitPanel />}\n        {activeTab === \"files\" && <FilesPanel />}\n      </Box>\n    </Box>\n  );\n}\n"
}

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	## Project
6	
7	clui is a TUI wrapper around the Claude Code SDK (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) providing multi-session tabs with process isolation, skills management, context tools, and git worktree support. Built with Ink 6 (React 19) for the terminal UI.
8	
9	## Architecture
10	
11	**Shell + Workers model:**
12	- **Shell process** — Main Ink/React TUI. Renders three-column layout (session sidebar, chat, skills sidebar), tab bar, input, status bar. UI state managed via Zustand. Spawns/supervises worker processes.
13	- **Worker processes** — One per tab. Each runs its own Claude Agent SDK instance in isolation. Communicates with shell via IPC over Unix Domain Sockets (JSON protocol).
14	- **SQLite** (`better-sqlite3`) — Shared persistence for sessions, messages, pins, snapshots, settings.
15	
16	Key directories:
17	- `src/shell/` — UI components, Zustand store slices, React hooks
18	- `src/worker/` — Per-tab worker: Claude SDK bridge, context manager, worktree manager
19	- `src/shared/` — Types, IPC protocol, DB helpers, config
20	- `src/cli/` — Argument parsing
21	- `db/migrations/` — SQLite migrations
22	
23	## Build & Dev Commands
24	
25	```bash
26	npm run build      # tsup → dist/
27	npm run dev        # tsup --watch
28	npm start          # node dist/index.js
29	npm test           # vitest
30	```
31	
32	Entry points: `src/index.tsx` (shell), `src/worker/index.ts` (worker). Both are separate tsup entry points — worker is forked via `child_process.fork()`.
33	
34	## Tech Stack
35	
36	TypeScript, Ink 6, React 19, Zustand, better-sqlite3, simple-git, tsup, vitest
37	
38	## Key Design Decisions
39	
40	- Workers are fully isolated — one crash doesn't affect shell or other tabs. Cross-tab context is opt-in via explicit IPC request.
41	- IPC uses Unix Domain Sockets (`node:net`), not stdin/stdout. JSON-framed messages.
42	- Skills have three-tier cascade: repo (`.claude/skills/`) > user (`~/.claude/skills/`) > global. Higher tier overrides same-named lower tier.
43	- Pins are either one-shot (next prompt only) or sticky (persists across prompts in session).
44	- `better-sqlite3` is external in tsup config (native module, can't be bundled).
45	
46	## Specs & Plans
47	
48	- Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-03-clui-design.md`
49	- Implementation plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-04-03-clui-implementation.md`

1	# clui — Design Specification
2	
3	> TUI wrapper around Claude Code with multi-session tabs, skills management, and context tools.
4	
5	## Overview
6	
7	clui is a terminal user interface that wraps the Claude Code SDK (`@anthropic-ai/claude-code`) to provide a richer development experience. It adds multi-session tabs with process isolation, a session history sidebar, a three-tier skills management sidebar, context management tools (pins, snapshots, compact indicator, reset), configurable status bar, and optional git worktree isolation per tab.
8	
9	## Architecture
10	
11	### Shell + Workers Model
12	
13	The app runs as two layers:
14	
15	- **Shell process** — the main Ink/React TUI. Renders the three-column layout, tab bar, sidebars, input, status bar. Manages UI state via Zustand. Spawns and supervises worker processes.
16	- **Worker processes** — one per tab/session. Each worker runs a Claude Code SDK instance in isolation. Communicates with the shell via IPC (Unix Domain Sockets). Manages its own context, pins, and optional git worktree.
17	
18	```
19	Shell (Ink/React)
20	  ├── UI Components (Layout, TabBar, Sidebars, ChatView, InputBar, StatusBar)
21	  ├── Zustand Store (tabs, sessions, skills, settings)
22	  ├── IPC Server (Unix Domain Socket)
23	  │
24	  ├── Worker 1 (Claude SDK + context manager + worktree manager)
25	  ├── Worker 2 (Claude SDK + context manager + worktree manager)
26	  └── Worker N ...
27	  │
28	  └── SQLite Database (shared: sessions, messages, snapshots, pins, settings)
29	```
30	
31	### Why Shell + Workers
32	
33	- **Isolation**: One worker crash does not kill the shell or other tabs.
34	- **Resource containment**: Each Claude SDK instance runs in its own process with its own memory.
35	- **Cross-tab opt-in**: Workers are isolated by default. Cross-tab context reading is an explicit IPC request, not shared state.
36	
37	## Tech Stack
38	
39	| Concern         | Choice                          | Rationale                                           |
40	|-----------------|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
41	| Language        | TypeScript                      | User preference, matches existing codebase          |
42	| TUI Framework   | Ink (React for CLI)             | Component model, hooks, familiar React patterns     |
43	| Agent SDK       | `@anthropic-ai/claude-code`     | Programmatic control, structured responses. API shape must be verified during Phase 1 — fallback to subprocess spawning if SDK doesn't expose needed events (streaming, compact notifications). |
44	| UI State        | Zustand                         | Lightweight, works with React, no boilerplate       |
45	| Database        | SQLite via `better-sqlite3`     | Single file, no server, good for local persistence  |
46	| IPC             | Unix Domain Sockets (`node:net`)| Fast, local-only, reliable                          |
47	| Git             | `simple-git`                    | Worktree management, diff stats, branch info        |
48	| Build           | tsup                            | Bundle to single distributable                      |
49	
50	## Layout
51	
52	Three-column layout with tab bar at top, context bar + input + status bar at bottom of center column.
53	
54	```
55	┌──────────┬──────────────────────────────────┬──────────────┐
56	│ Sessions │  [Tab1: fix-auth] [Tab2: refactor] [+]         │ Skills       │
57	│          ├──────────────────────────────────┤              │
58	│ ● fix-auth│                                │ ▼ Repo       │
59	│   refactor│  Chat output (streaming)       │   ☑ tdd      │
60	│   chat-3  │                                │   ☑ nestjs   │
61	│          │                                  │   ☐ db       │
62	│          │                                  │ ▶ User       │
63	│          │                                  │ ▶ Global     │
64	│          ├──────────────────────────────────┤              │
65	│          │ 📌 src/auth.ts | 📌 tdd (sticky)│              │
66	│          │ 1️⃣ nestjs-skill | /commit        │              │
67	│          ├──────────────────────────────────┤              │
68	│          │ > _                              │              │
69	│          ├──────────────────────────────────┤              │
70	│          │ Opus 4.6 | Ctx: 31k/1M (3%) | $0.31 | main    │              │
71	└──────────┴──────────────────────────────────┴──────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	## Components
75	
76	### 1. Session Sidebar (Left)
77	
78	- **Data source**: Claude Code session API (reuse existing session data).
79	- **Display**: List of sessions with name, date, cost, duration.
80	- **Color tags**: User assigns a color dot to any session. Stored in SQLite.
```

  "new_string": "# CLAUDE.md\n\nThis file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.\n\n## Project\n\nclui is a TUI wrapper around the Claude Code SDK (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) providing multi-session tabs with process isolation, skills management, context tools, and git worktree support. 75	
76	## Components
77	
78	### 1. Session Sidebar (Left)
79	
80	- **Data source**: Claude Code session API (reuse existing session data).
81	- **Display**: List of sessions with name, date, cost, duration.
82	- **Color tags**: User assigns a color dot to any session. Stored in SQLite.
83	- **Rename**: Inline rename (select + type). Stored in SQLite as override.
84	- **Search**: Filter sessions by name/date.
85	- **Actions**: Click to open in new tab. Right-arrow or Enter to resume.
86	- **Ordering**: Most recent first.
87	
88	### 2. Tab Bar (Top of center column)
89	
90	- **Tabs represent sessions**. Each tab = one worker process.
91	- **Naming**: Auto-indexed (`1`, `2`, `3`...) + session name (from task, user-given, or auto).
92	- **Creation**: `[+]` button or hotkey.
93	- **Switching**: Click tab or hotkey (e.g., Ctrl+1..9, Ctrl+Tab).
94	- **Closing**: Close button on tab.
95	  - No worktree → close immediately, worker killed.
96	  - Has worktree → prompt: "Close and keep worktree" or "Close and clean up worktree".
97	- **No tab limit**.
98	
99	### 3. Skills Sidebar (Right)
100	
101	Three collapsible tiers with cascade priority:
102	
103	1. **Repo** (open by default) — skills from `.claude/skills/` in current repo. Highest priority.
104	2. **User** (collapsed) — skills from `~/.claude/skills/`. Overridden by repo.
105	3. **Global** (collapsed) — bundled/system skills. Overridden by both.
106	
107	**Visual rules**:
108	- Active skills: normal text, full color.
109	- Overridden skills (same name exists in higher tier): greyed out, non-interactive.
110	- Each skill has a pin button next to it.
111	
112	**Pin interaction**:
113	- Click pin → add to context bar as one-shot (used for next prompt only).
114	- Modifier+click (e.g., Shift+click) → add as sticky (persists across prompts).
115	- Same interaction pattern for files and commands.
116	
117	### 4. Context Bar (Above Input)
118	
119	Unified view of everything attached to the current/next prompt:
120	
121	- **Sticky items** (📌): Pinned files and skills that persist across all prompts in this session.
122	- **One-shot items** (1️⃣): Files, skills, commands attached for the next prompt only. Auto-removed after send.
123	- **Selected capabilities**: Any skill or command selected from the sidebar.
124	- **Click to remove** any item.
125	- **Quick-add in input**: Type `@filepath` to pin a file, `/skill-name` to pin a skill.
126	
127	### 5. Input Bar
128	
129	- Text input with multiline support.
130	- Sends to active tab's worker via IPC.
131	- Context bar items are prepended to the prompt as system context.
132	
133	### 6. Status Bar (Below Input)
134	
135	- **User-configurable**: Settings UI to toggle which fields to show.
136	- **Available fields**:
137	  - Model name and context window size
138	  - Total tokens used in session
139	  - Current context usage (absolute + percentage)
140	  - Style/persona name
141	  - Session ID
142	  - Session duration (live timer)
143	  - Session cost
144	  - Git branch name
145	  - Git diff stats (+added, -removed, ~modified)
146	- **Auto-compact indicator**: Icon/flash in status bar when context compression occurs. Expandable to show what was dropped.
147	
148	## Context Management
149	
150	### Pin System
151	
152	Two modes:
153	- **Per-prompt (one-shot)**: Attached to the next prompt only. Removed after sending.
```

ok claude what king of cappabilities can i use in the prompt? skills afiles, what else?

> AGENT

Based on the current codebase, here's what you can attach to a prompt:

**Implemented:**
- **Files** — `@filepath` in input → pins a file as context
- **Skills** — `/skill-name` in input → pins a skill as context
- **Pin modes** — one-shot (next prompt only) or sticky (persists across prompts)

**Pin types in the type system** (`shared/types.ts`):
- `file` — a file path
- `skill` — a skill name
- That's it currently. The `PinType` is `"file" | "skill"`.

**Not yet implemented but could be added:**
- **Directories** — `@dir/` to include a directory tree
- **URLs** — `@https://...` to fetch and attach web content
- **MCP tools** — attach specific MCP server tools
- **Hooks** — attach hook outputs
- **Git context** — `@diff`, `@branch`, `@commit:sha` to attach git state
- **Snippets** — `@file:L10-L50` for specific line ranges
- **Commands** — `!command` to run a shell command and attach output
- **Images** — `@image.png` for multimodal context

Which of these do you want to add to the context bar system?

> DEVELOPER

i mean in the real claude code

> AGENT

In real Claude Code, you can attach to prompts:

- **Files** — `@filepath` or drag-and-drop
- **Directories** — `@dir/`
- **URLs** — `@https://...`
- **Git diffs** — `@diff`, `@git:sha`
- **Images** — paste or `@image.png`
- **Skills/Slash commands** — `/skill-name`
- **MCP resources** — from connected MCP servers

That's the core set from the CLI. The SDK we're wrapping (`@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk`) would pass these as context to the agent.

Want me to expand our `PinType` and context bar to support all of these?

Each session JSONL file contains full conversation data:

**Per message:**
- `type`: `"user"` or `"assistant"`
- `message.content`: full text (user prompts, assistant responses)
- `message.model`: model used (e.g. `claude-opus-4-6`)
- `timestamp`: when sent
- `cwd`: working directory
- `gitBranch`: active branch
- `usage`: tokens (input, output, cache), cost info
- `version`: Claude Code version
- `entrypoint`: how it was invoked

**What we could show in sessions list:**
- First user message as session title/summary
- Model used
- Token count / cost (from usage)
- Git branch at time of session
- Message count
- Duration (first → last timestamp)

27	export function SessionSidebar({
28	  onOpenSession,
29	  visible,
30	}: SessionSidebarProps): React.ReactElement {
31	  const sessions = useStore((s) => s.sessions);
32	  const sessionFilter = useStore((s) => s.sessionFilter);
33	  const updateSessionColor = useStore((s) => s.updateSessionColor);
34	  const updateSessionName = useStore((s) => s.updateSessionName);
35	
36	  const [selectedIdx, setSelectedIdx] = useState(0);
37	  const [renaming, setRenaming] = useState<string | null>(null);
38	  const [renameValue, setRenameValue] = useState("");
39	
40	  const filtered = sessionFilter
41	    ? sessions.filter((s) => s.name.toLowerCase().includes(sessionFilter.toLowerCase()))
42	    : sessions;
43	
44	  useInput(
45	    (input, key) => {
46	      if (!visible) return;
47	
48	      // Rename mode — capture all input for rename
49	      if (renaming) {
50	        if (key.return) {
51	          if (renameValue.trim()) {
52	            updateSessionName(renaming, renameValue.trim());
53	          }
54	          setRenaming(null);
55	          setRenameValue("");
56	          return;
57	        }
58	        if (key.escape) {
59	          setRenaming(null);
60	          setRenameValue("");
61	          return;
62	        }
63	        if (key.backspace || key.delete) {
64	          setRenameValue((v) => v.slice(0, -1));
65	          return;
66	        }
67	        if (input && !key.ctrl && !key.meta) {
68	          setRenameValue((v) => v + input);
69	        }
70	        return;
71	      }
72	
73	      if (key.upArrow) {
74	        setSelectedIdx((i) => Math.max(0, i - 1));
75	        return;
76	      }
77	      if (key.downArrow) {
78	        setSelectedIdx((i) => Math.min(filtered.length - 1, i + 1));
79	        return;
80	      }
81	      if (key.return && filtered[selectedIdx]) {
82	        onOpenSession(filtered[selectedIdx]);
83	        return;
84	      }
85	      if (input === "r" && filtered[selectedIdx]) {
86	        setRenaming(filtered[selectedIdx].id);
87	        setRenameValue(filtered[selectedIdx].name);
88	        return;
89	      }
90	      if (input === "c" && filtered[selectedIdx]) {
91	        const session = filtered[selectedIdx];
92	        const currentIdx = COLORS.indexOf(session.color || "");
93	        const nextColor = COLORS[(currentIdx + 1) % COLORS.length];
94	        updateSessionColor(session.id, nextColor);
95	        return;
96	      }
97	    },
98	    { isActive: visible }
99	  );
100	
101	  if (!visible) return <></>;
102	
103	  return (
104	    <Box flexDirection="column" paddingX={1} flexGrow={1}>
105	      <Box flexDirection="column" flexGrow={1} overflow="hidden">
106	      {filtered.map((session, idx) => {
107	        const isSelected = idx === selectedIdx;
108	        const isRenaming = renaming === session.id;
109	
110	        return (
111	          <Box key={session.id} flexDirection="column" marginBottom={1}>
112	            <Box flexDirection="row">
113	              <Text color={session.color || "white"}>
114	                {isSelected ? "> " : "  "}
115	              </Text>
116	              {isRenaming ? (
117	                <Text color="cyan">{renameValue}<Text inverse> </Text></Text>
118	              ) : (
119	                <Text
120	                  color={isSelected ? "white" : "gray"}
121	                  bold={isSelected}
122	                  wrap="truncate"
123	                >
124	                  {session.name}
125	                </Text>
126	              )}
127	            </Box>
128	            <Text color="gray" dimColor>
129	              {"    "}{formatDate(session.createdAt)}
130	            </Text>
131	          </Box>
132	        );
133	      })}
134	
135	      {filtered.length === 0 && (
136	        <Text color="gray">No sessions found</Text>
137	      )}
138	      </Box>
139	
140	      <Box flexShrink={0} paddingTop={1}>
141	        <Text color="gray" dimColor>
142	          up/dn | Enter | r rename | c color
143	        </Text>
144	      </Box>
145	    </Box>
146	  );
147	}
148	
```
