featureBar(3) - sidebar borders(2) - tab buttons(3) - marginTop(1) - hints(2)\n  const termHeight = stdout?.rows ?? 40;\n  const availableHeight = termHeight - 3 - 2 - 3 - 1 - 2;\n  const visibleCount = Math.max(1, Math.floor(availableHeight / TILE_HEIGHT));\n\n  // Keep selected item in view\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (selectedIdx < scrollOffset) {\n      setScrollOffset(selectedIdx);\n    } else if (selectedIdx >= scrollOffset + visibleCount) {\n      setScrollOffset(selectedIdx - visibleCount + 1);\n    }\n  }, [selectedIdx, visibleCount]);\n\n  const pageSize = Math.max(1, visibleCount - 1);\n\n  useInput(\n    (input, key) => {\n      if (!visible) return;\n\n      if (renaming) {\n        if (key.return) {\n          if (renameValue.trim()) {\n            updateSessionName(renaming, renameValue.trim());\n          }\n          setRenaming(null);\n          setRenameValue(\"\");\n          return;\n        }\n        if (key.escape) {\n          setRenaming(null);\n          setRenameValue(\"\");\n          return;\n        }\n        if (key.backspace || key.delete) {\n          setRenameValue((v) => v.slice(0, -1));\n          return;\n        }\n        if (input && !key.ctrl && !key.meta) {\n          setRenameValue((v) => v + input);\n        }\n        return;\n      }\n\n      if (key.upArrow) {\n        setSelectedIdx((i) => Math.max(0, i - 1));\n        return;\n      }\n      if (key.downArrow) {\n        setSelectedIdx((i) => Math.min(filtered.length - 1, i + 1));\n        return;\n      }\n      // Page Up / Page Down via Ctrl+U / Ctrl+D (vim-style)\n      if (key.ctrl && input === \"d\") {\n        setSelectedIdx((i) => Math.min(filtered.length - 1, i + pageSize));\n        return;\n      }\n      if (key.ctrl && input === \"b\") {\n        setSelectedIdx((i) => Math.max(0, i - pageSize));\n        return;\n      }\n      if (key.return && filtered[selectedIdx]) {\n        onOpenSession(filtered[selectedIdx]);\n        return;\n      }\n      if (input === \"r\" && filtered[selectedIdx]) {\n        setRenaming(filtered[selectedIdx].id);\n        setRenameValue(filtered[selectedIdx].name);\n        return;\n      }\n      if (input === \"c\" && filtered[selectedIdx]) {\n        const session = filtered[selectedIdx];\n        const currentIdx = COLORS.indexOf(session.color || \"\");\n        const nextColor = COLORS[(currentIdx + 1) % COLORS.length];\n        updateSessionColor(session.id, nextColor);\n        return;\n      }\n    },\n    { isActive: visible }\n  );\n\n  // Mouse scroll in sidebar area\n  const handleMouse = useCallback(\n    (event: MouseEvent) => {\n      if (!visible) return;\n      if (event.x >= leftW) return; // outside sidebar\n\n      if (event.button === \"scrollUp\") {\n        setSelectedIdx((i) => Math.max(0, i - 6	 * Top bar — full width, holds session tabs.

```
8	export function FeatureBar(): React.ReactElement {
9	  const tabs = useStore((s) => s.tabs);
10	  const activeTabId = useStore((s) => s.activeTabId);
11	  const setActiveTab = useStore((s) => s.setActiveTab);
12	  const createTab = useStore((s) => s.createTab);
13	  const closeTab = useStore((s) => s.closeTab);
14	
15	  useInput((input, key) => {
16	    if (input === "t" && key.ctrl) {
17	      createTab();
18	      return;
19	    }
20	    if (input === "w" && key.ctrl && activeTabId) {
21	      closeTab(activeTabId);
22	      return;
23	    }
24	    if (key.ctrl && input >= "1" && input <= "9") {
25	      const idx = parseInt(input, 10) - 1;
26	      if (tabs[idx]) {
27	        setActiveTab(tabs[idx].id);
28	      }
29	      return;
30	    }
31	    if (key.tab && !key.shift && tabs.length > 1) {
32	      const currentIdx = tabs.findIndex((t) => t.id === activeTabId);
33	      const nextIdx = (currentIdx + 1) % tabs.length;
34	      setActiveTab(tabs[nextIdx].id);
35	    }
36	  });
37	
38	  return (
39	    <Box
40	      flexDirection="row"
41	      borderStyle="round"
42	      borderColor="gray"
43	      paddingX={1}
44	      flexShrink={0}
45	      height={3}
46	    >
47	      {tabs.map((tab) => (
48	        <Box key={tab.id} paddingX={1}>
49	          <Text
50	            color={tab.id === activeTabId ? "cyan" : "gray"}
51	            bold={tab.id === activeTabId}
52	          >
53	            {tab.index}: {tab.name}
54	          </Text>
55	        </Box>
56	      ))}
57	      <Box paddingX={1}>
58	        <Text color="green">[+]</Text>
59	      </Box>
60	    </Box>
61	  );
62	}
```

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/clui/src/shell/components/FeatureBar.tsx",
  "content": "import React, { useEffect, useCallback } from \"react\";\nimport { Box, Text, useInput } from \"ink\";\nimport { useStore } from \"../store/index.js\";\nimport { mouseEvents, type MouseEvent } from \"../mouseStream.js\";\n\n/**\n * Top bar — full width. Tabs on the left, sidebar toggle buttons on the right.\n */\nexport function FeatureBar(): React.ReactElement {\n  const tabs = useStore((s) => s.tabs);\n  const activeTabId = useStore((s) => s.activeTabId);\n  const setActiveTab = useStore((s) => s.setActiveTab);\n  const createTab = useStore((s) => s.createTab);\n  const closeTab = useStore((s) => s.closeTab);\n  const leftVisible = useStore((s) => s.leftSidebarVisible);\n  const rightVisible = useStore((s) => s.rightSidebarVisible);\n  const toggleLeft = useStore((s) => s.toggleLeftSidebar);\n  const toggleRight = useStore((s) => s.toggleRightSidebar);\n\n  useInput((input, key) => {\n    if (input === \"t\" && key.ctrl) {\n      createTab();\n      return;\n    }\n    if (input === \"w\" && key.ctrl && activeTabId) {\n      closeTab(activeTabId);\n      return;\n    }\n    if (key.ctrl && input >= \"1\" && input <= \"9\") {\n      const idx = parseInt(input, 10) - 1;\n      if (tabs[idx]) {\n        setActiveTab(tabs[idx].id);\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n    if (key.tab && !key.shift && tabs.length > 1) {\n      const currentIdx = tabs.findIndex((t) => t.id === activeTabId);\n      const nextIdx = (currentIdx + 1) % tabs.length;\n      setActiveTab(tabs[nextIdx].id);\n    }\n  });\n\n  // Mouse click on toggle buttons (right side of top bar)\n  // Buttons are at Y=1 (inside border), far right\n  const handleMouse = useCallback(\n    (event: MouseEvent) => {\n      if (event.type !== \"press\" || event.button !== \"left\") return;\n      if (event.y !== 1) return; // only the content row of the top bar\n\n      const termWidth = process.stdout.columns ?? 120;\n      // Right-side buttons: \"  [sidebar icon] [sidebar icon]  \" at the far right\n      // Each button is ~4 chars, with padding. Positioned from the right.\n      // Layout: ... | [left toggle] [right toggle] |border(1)| padding(1)\n      const rightBtnX = termWidth - 3; // \"]\" of right button\n      const leftBtnX = termWidth - 7;  // \"]\" of left button\n\n      if (event.x >= termWidth - 5 && event.x <= termWidth - 2) {\n        toggleRight();\n      } else if (event.x >= termWidth - 9 && event.x <= termWidth - 6) {\n        toggleLeft();\n      }\n    },\n    [toggleLeft, toggleRight]\n  );\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    mouseEvents.on(\"mouse\", handleMouse);\n    return () => { mouseEvents.off(\"mouse\", handleMouse); };\n  }, [handleMouse]);\n\n  return (\n    <Box\n      flexDirection=\"row\"\n      borderStyle=\"round\"\n      borderColor=\"gray\"\n      paddingX={1}\n      flexShrink={0}\n      height={3}\n    >\n      {/* Tabs - left side */}\n      <Box flexDirection=\"row\" flexGrow={1}>\n        {tabs.map((tab) => (\n          <Box key={tab.id} paddingX={1}>\n            <Text\n              color={tab.id === activeTabId ? \"cyan\" : \"gray\"}\n              bold={tab.id === activeTabId}\n            >\n              {tab.index}: {tab.name}\n            </Text>\n          </Box>\n        ))}\n        <Box paddingX={1}>\n          <Text color=\"green\">[+]</Text>\n        </Box>\n      </Box>\n\n      {/* Sidebar toggle buttons - right side */}\n      <Box flexDirection=\"row\" flexShrink={0}>\n        <Box paddingX={1}>\n          <Text color={leftVisible ? \"cyan\" : \"gray\"}>\n            {leftVisible ? \"[<]\" : \"[>]\"}\n          </Text>\n        </Box>\n        <Box paddingX={1}>\n          <Text color={rightVisible ? \"cyan\" : \"gray\"}>\n            {rightVisible ? \"[>]\" : \"[<]\"}\n          </Text>\n        </Box>\n      </Box>\n    </Box>\n  );\n}\n"
}
```

> AGENT

The issue: `toggleLeft` and `toggleRight` are Zustand selectors that return new function references on every render, causing `handleMouse` to be recreated constantly. The `useEffect` cleans up the old listener and adds a new one, but during the gap, clicks get lost.

Also the click coordinate ranges are hardcoded and likely wrong — they don't account for the actual rendered button positions.

Fix: don't use selectors for the toggle functions in the callback — call `useStore.getState()` directly inside the handler. And fix the click detection to be more robust.

> AGENT

Fixed. Two problems:

1. **Stale closures** — `toggleLeft`/`toggleRight` were Zustand selectors passed as useCallback deps. They created new function refs on every render, causing the event listener to constantly detach/reattach. Now uses `useStore.getState().toggleLeftSidebar()` directly inside the handler with `[]` deps — stable, never recreates.

2. **Click coordinate math** — recalculated the X ranges based on the actual rendered layout from the right edge.

> AGENT

Here's what a developer opening our ADE would expect but doesn't have yet:

**Critical (core workflow blockers):**
- **File tree** — Files tab is empty. Need actual project tree with click-to-pin
- **Agent activity feed** — when agent works, show live: which files read/written, tools used, thinking indicator, progress
- **Streaming chat** — code blocks need syntax highlighting, tool calls need collapsible sections
- **Cancel/interrupt** — Ctrl+C or button to stop the agent mid-response

**High value (daily use):**
- **Git diff viewer** — Git tab just shows branch name. Need staged/unstaged files, inline diffs
- **Search** — Ctrl+F to search sessions, files, code
- **Model selector** — switch models from UI (dropdown or hotkey)
- **Keyboard shortcuts overlay** — `?` to show all keybindings
- **Cost/token budget** — alerts when approaching limits

**Nice to have (polish):**
- **Split view** — view file + chat side by side
- **Command palette** — Ctrl+P fuzzy finder for everything
- **Notifications** — context window warnings, compact events
- **Session auto-naming** — AI-generated summary titles
- **Theme** — dark/light, color customization
- **Scroll in chat** — mouse wheel + Page Up/Down
- **Copy code blocks** — click to copy from chat output

**The biggest gap is the Files tab and agent activity feed.** A developer spends most time navigating files and watching what the agent does. Without those, the ADE feels hollow.

Which ones do you want to tackle?

```json
  "content": "import React, { useState, useEffect, useCallback } from \"react\";\nimport { Box, Text, useInput, useStdout } from \"ink\";\nimport { mouseEvents, type MouseEvent } from \"../mouseStream.js\";\nimport { useStore } from \"../store/index.js\";\nimport type { Pin } from \"../../shared/types.js\";\n\ninterface ContextBarProps {\n  pins: Pin[];\n}\n\nexport function ContextBar({ pins }: ContextBarProps): React.ReactElement {\n  const [selectedPinIdx, setSelectedPinIdx] = useState(-1); // -1 = no pin selected\n  const { stdout } = useStdout();\n  const leftW = useStore((s) => s.leftSidebarWidth);\n  const rightW = useStore((s) => s.rightSidebarWidth);\n  const termWidth = stdout?.columns ?? 120;\n\n  const hasPins = pins.length > 0;\n  const contentLines = hasPins ? Math.min(3, Math.ceil(pins.length / 3)) : 1;\n  const height = contentLines + 1;\n\n  // Reset selection when pins change\n  useEffect(() => {\n    if (selectedPinIdx >= pins.length) setSelectedPinIdx(Math.max(-1, pins.length - 1));\n  }, [pins.length]);\n\n  // Keyboard: Alt+Left/Right to navigate pins, Delete/Backspace to remove\n  useInput((input, key) => {\n    if (!hasPins) return;\n\n    // Alt+[ and Alt+] to navigate pins (won't conflict with input)\n    if (key.meta && input === \"[\") {\n      setSelectedPinIdx((i) => Math.max(0, i - 1));\n      return;\n    }\n    if (key.meta && input === \"]\") {\n      setSelectedPinIdx((i) => Math.min(pins.length - 1, i + 1));\n      return;\n    }\n    // Alt+X to remove selected pin\n    if (key.meta && input === \"x\") {\n      if (selectedPinIdx >= 0 && selectedPinIdx < pins.length) {\n        const pin = pins[selectedPinIdx];\n        const tabId = useStore.getState().activeTabId;\n        if (tabId) useStore.getState().removePin(tabId, pin.id);\n      }\n      return;\n    }\n  });\n\n  // Mouse: click on a pin's x button to remove\n  const handleMouse = useCallback(\n    (event: MouseEvent) => {\n      if (!hasPins) return;\n      if (event.type !== \"press\" || event.button !== \"left\") return;\n\n      // Context bar Y position: above the input, below chat\n      // It's rendered in the center column, so X must be within [leftW, termWidth - rightW]\n      if (event.x < leftW || event.x >= termWidth - rightW) return;\n\n      // Context bar is near the bottom. Exact Y is hard to compute,\n      // but we can check if the click is in the right general area.\n      // Each pin renders as: \"icon target [x] \" with marginRight\n      // We'll compute pin positions from left to right\n      let xPos = leftW + 2; // border(1) + paddingX(1)\n\n      for (let i = 0; i < pins.length; i++) {\n        const pin = pins[i];\n        const icon = pin.type === \"skill\" ? \"⚡\" : pin.type === \"file\" ? \"📄\" : \"📁\";\n        // Pin text: \"icon target [x] \" — icon(2) + space(1) + target + space(1) + [x](3) + marginRight(1)\n        const targetLen = pin.target.length;\n        const pinWidth = 2 + 1 + targetLen + 1 + 3 + 1;\n\n        // [x] is at the end of the pin, 4 chars from the pin's right edge\n        const xStart = xPos + pinWidth - 5; // start of \" [x]\"\n        const xEnd = xPos + pinWidth - 2;   // end of \"[x]\"\n\n        if (event.x >= xStart && event.x <= xEnd) {\n          const tabId = useStore.getState().activeTabId;\n          if (tabId) useStore.getState().removePin(tabId, pin.id);\n          return;\n        }\n\n        // Click anywhere on pin selects it\n        if (event.x >= xPos && event.x < xPos + pinWidth) {\n          setSelectedPinIdx(i);\n          return;\n        }\n\n        xPos += pinWidth;\n      }\n    },\n    [hasPins, pins, leftW, rightW, termWidth]\n  );\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    mouseEvents.on(\"mouse\", handleMouse);\n    return () => { mouseEvents.off(\"mouse\", handleMouse); };\n  }, [handleMouse]);\n\n  return (\n    <Box\n      flexDirection=\"row\"\n      flexWrap=\"wrap\"\n      paddingX={1}\n      borderStyle=\"round\"\n      borderColor=\"gray\"\n      borderBottom={false}\n      flexShrink={0}\n      height={height}\n    >\n      {hasPins ? (\n        <>\n          {pins.map((pin, idx) => {\n            const isSelected = idx === selectedPinIdx;\n            const isSticky = pin.mode === \"sticky\";\n            const color = isSticky ? \"cyan\" : \"yellow\";\n            const icon = pin.type === \"skill\" ? \"⚡\" : pin.type === \"file\" ? \"📄\" : \"📁\";\n\n            return (\n              <Box key={pin.id} marginRight={1}>\n                <Text color={color} bold={isSelected}>\n                  {icon} {pin.target}\n                </Text>\n                {isSelected && (\n                  <Text color=\"red\"> [x]</Text>\n                )}\n                {!isSticky && !isSelected && (\n                  <Text dimColor> (1x)</Text>\n                )}\n              </Box>\n            );\n          })}\n        </>\n      ) : (\n        <Text dimColor>No context attached — use @file or /skill to pin</Text>\n      )}\n    </Box>\n  );\n}\n"
```

The problem is likely that `togglePin` calls `useStore.getState()` which triggers re-renders, and with many pins the `activePins` selector causes cascading updates. Also, the `handleMouse` callback has `flat` in its deps which recreates on every render since `flat` is recomputed each time.

Let me fix all three issues:

> AGENT

The "stops after 4" bug: the `tabPins` selector returns the array directly from the store. When pins change, `tabPins` gets a new reference, `pinnedPaths` recalculates, component re-renders, `handleAltP` recreates (depends on `selectedIdx`), effect re-runs. But the `handleAltP` dep on `selectedIdx` means it captures a stale `selectedIdx` after rapid re-renders.

The real issue: `handleAltP` uses `selectedIdx` directly. After pinning, the re-render cascade might reset something. Let me use a ref for selectedIdx in the handler.

> TOOL

The state is local (`useState`) so it resets when the component unmounts (tab switch). Need to move `expanded`, `selectedIdx`, `scrollOffset` to module-level or Zustand store.

Simplest approach: module-level variables that persist across mounts. The tree itself should also be cached.

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01KWXfCtx98Fj2r3gSovbyG4
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/clui/src/shell/components/FilesPanel.tsx",
  "old_string": "export function FilesPanel(): React.ReactElement {\n  const rootDir = process.cwd();\n  const [tree, setTree] = useState<FileNode[]>([]);\n  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set([rootDir]));\n  const [selectedIdx, setSelectedIdx] = useState(0);\n  const [hoverIdx, setHoverIdx] = useState(-1);\n  const [scrollOffset, setScrollOffset] = useState(0);",
  "new_string": "// Persist file tree state across tab switches / unmounts\nconst ROOT_DIR = process.cwd();\nlet persistedTree: FileNode[] | null = null;\nlet persistedExpanded = new Set<string>([ROOT_DIR]);\nlet persistedSelectedIdx = 0;\nlet persistedScrollOffset = 0;\n\nexport function FilesPanel(): React.ReactElement {\n  const rootDir = ROOT_DIR;\n  const [tree, setTree] = useState<FileNode[]>(() => {\n    if (persistedTree) return persistedTree;\n    const t = buildTree(rootDir, 0, 1);\n    persistedTree = t;\n    return t;\n  });\n  const [expanded, setExpanded] = useState<Set<string>>(() => persistedExpanded);\n  const [selectedIdx, setSelectedIdx] = useState(() => persistedSelectedIdx);\n  const [hoverIdx, setHoverIdx] = useState(-1);\n  const [scrollOffset, setScrollOffset] = useState(() => persistedScrollOffset);\n\n  // Sync state back to module-level on every change\n  useEffect(() => { persistedTree = tree; }, [tree]);\n  useEffect(() => { persistedExpanded = expanded; }, [expanded]);\n  useEffect(() => { persistedSelectedIdx = selectedIdx; }, [selectedIdx]);\n  useEffect(() => { persistedScrollOffset = scrollOffset; }, [scrollOffset]);"
}
```

> AGENT

Yes, we're in the same space. But there are important differences:

**What most of those tools are:**
- **Parallel agent runners** — tmux/worktree wrappers that spawn multiple agents and show their output side-by-side (claude-squad, dmux, amux, crystal)
- **Kanban/task boards** — assign tickets to agents (dorothy, agent-kanban, openkanban)
- **Agent swarms** — multi-agent coordination protocols (claude-flow, swarm-protocol)

**What clui is:**
- A **full IDE-like shell** wrapping the Claude SDK — not just a tmux splitter
- Custom input editor with selection, multiline, keyboard shortcuts
- File tree browser with pin-to-context
- Skills/MCP management panels
- Mouse-driven resizable panels
- Session history from actual Claude data

**Our position in this landscape:**
- Closest to: `1code`, `jat`, `constellagent`, `superset` — the ones calling themselves "IDE" or "terminal built for agents"
- We go deeper on the **UI/UX layer** than most (custom input, mouse support, context management)
- We're weaker on **multi-agent orchestration** — we have tabs/workers but no swarm coordination, no kanban, no parallel worktree execution

**What we should steal from this list:**
1. **Git worktree per agent** (crystal, dmux, aizen) — we have the architecture but it's not wired up yet
2. **Diff viewer** (parallel-code) — see what the agent changed
3. **Kanban/task board** (dorothy, agent-kanban) — assign tasks to agents visually
4. **Agent activity monitoring** — most of these show real-time agent status

We're building a **premium ADE**, not a tmux wrapper. The differentiator is the polished UI and deep context management. Want to keep pushing on that path or pivot toward multi-agent orchestration?

> DEVELOPER

[Image #31] check white it is selection... it selects all in the terminal

> AGENT

Cmd+A is being intercepted by the **terminal emulator** (Ghostty) itself — it selects all terminal output before our app even sees the keypress. The `\x1ba` sequence never reaches our stdin.

This is a terminal-level behavior we can't override from inside the app. The fix has to be on the terminal side — Ghostty needs to be configured to pass Cmd+A through instead of handling it.

In Ghostty config (`~/.config/ghostty/config`):

```
keybind = super+a=text:\x1ba
```

This tells Ghostty to send `ESC+a` to the app instead of doing native select-all.

Want me to add this to the project docs as a recommended Ghostty config? Or should we use a different keybinding for select-all that doesn't conflict (like Ctrl+Shift+A)?

Done. File viewer is implemented:

**Opening files:**
- **Enter** or **click** on a file in the file tree → opens in a new tab
- If file is already open → switches to that tab (no duplicates)
- Tab shows `📄` icon + filename in the top bar

**File viewer features:**
- **Line numbers** on the left (gray)
- **Syntax highlighting** for: TypeScript/JS (keywords, strings, numbers, comments), JSON (keys vs values), Markdown (headers, lists, code fences), YAML (keys, comments)
- **Read-only** — no editing, just viewing
- **Scroll**: arrow keys (1 line), Ctrl+D/B (page), mouse wheel (3 lines)
- **Header**: filename, line count, extension, current line range
- **Ctrl+W** closes file tabs like session tabs

> AGENT

The Y coordinate calculation is wrong. The `contentStartY = 3` doesn't account for the FeatureBar (top tab bar) and the file info header bar. Let me fix the offset.

FeatureBar: 3 rows. Then the center column starts. Inside center: InfoBar (TabBar) takes ~3 rows, then FileViewer starts. FileViewer's own header (file info) takes 3 rows. So content starts at Y = 3 (featureBar) + 3 (infoBar) + 3 (file header) = 9.

> AGENT

The problem: Ctrl+C sends `\x03` which Ink interprets as exit signal (we have `exitOnCtrlC: true` in render). And Cmd+C never reaches the app — Ghostty intercepts it.

Fix: use OSC 52 to push to clipboard automatically when selection changes, so the user doesn't need to press anything — just select and it's already copied. This is how modern terminals work.

120;\n  const rightW = useStore((s) => s.rightSidebarWidth);\n  const rightVisible = useStore((s) => s.rightSidebarVisible);\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const handler = (n: NotificationData) => {\n      setNotifications((prev) => [...prev, n]);\n\n      setTimeout(() => {\n        setNotifications((prev) => prev.filter((x) => x.id !== n.id));\n      }, n.duration || 3000);\n    };\n\n    listeners.add(handler);\n    return () => { listeners.delete(handler); };\n  }, []);\n\n  if (notifications.length === 0) return <></>;\n\n  // Position: top-right, below the FeatureBar (row 3)\n  // Width: fit content, max 40 chars\n  const maxWidth = 40;\n\n  return (\n    <Box\n      position=\"absolute\"\n      marginTop={3}\n      marginLeft={termWidth - maxWidth - (rightVisible ? rightW : 0) - 1}\n      flexDirection=\"column\"\n      width={maxWidth}\n    >\n      {notifications.map((n) => (\n        <Box\n          key={n.id}\n          borderStyle=\"round\"\n          borderColor={n.color || \"green\"}\n          paddingX={1}\n          marginBottom={1}\n        >\n          <Text color={n.color || \"green\"}>{n.message}</Text>\n        </Box>\n      ))}\n    </Box>\n  );\n}\n"
```json
}
```

Done. Notification system implemented:

**Notification popup:**
- Appears top-right, below the tab bar
- Rounded border, color-coded (green for copy, cyan for pin, yellow for unpin)
- Auto-dismisses after 2-3 seconds
- Stacks if multiple notifications appear

**Triggers:**
- **Copy text in file viewer** → "Copied N lines to clipboard"
- **Ctrl+A in file viewer** → "Copied entire file (N lines)"
- **Pin file/dir** → "Pinned filename to context"
- **Unpin file/dir** → "Unpinned filename"

Use `notify(message, color, duration)` from any component to show notifications.

```
9	  const refresh = useCallback(async () => {
10	    if (!activeTabId) return;
11	
12	    try {
13	      const git = simpleGit(cwd);

19

25	        gitDiffStats: {
26	          added: diffSummary.insertions,
27	          removed: diffSummary.deletions,
28	          modified: diffSummary.changed,
29	        },
30	      });

32	      updateTabStatus(activeTabId, { gitBranch: null, gitDiffStats: null });

34	  }, [cwd, activeTabId, updateTabStatus]);
```

**Git Panel (left sidebar → Git tab):**

- Two-column line numbers (old line / new line)
- Color-coded: `+` green (additions), `-` red (deletions), context in gray
- Hunk headers (`@@`) in cyan bold
- Untracked files show as all-additions
- Scroll: arrows, Ctrl+D/B, mouse wheel
- Closes with Ctrl+W like any tab

realIdx : prev);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      if (event.type === \"press\" && event.button === \"left\") {\n        setSelectedIdx(realIdx);\n        const item = flatRef.current[realIdx];\n        if (!item) return;\n\n        if (item.type === \"section\") {\n          setExpandedSections((prev) => {\n            const next = new Set(prev);\n            if (next.has(item.section)) next.delete(item.section);\n            else next.add(item.section);\n            return next;\n          });\n          return;\n        }\n\n        // Action buttons are on the right side of the row\n        // Layout from right: \"|border\" - \"x\"(discard) - \"+\"(stage/unstage) - \"o\"(open)\n        // Each button is ~2 chars, right-aligned\n        const actionsStartX = lw - 10;\n\n        if (event.x >= actionsStartX) {\n          const btnIdx = Math.floor((event.x - actionsStartX) / 3);\n          if (!item.file.staged) {\n            // Unstaged: [open] [stage] [discard]\n            if (btnIdx === 0) openFile(item.file);\n            else if (btnIdx === 1) stageFile(item.file);\n            else if (btnIdx === 2) discardFile(item.file);\n          } else {\n            // Staged: [open] [unstage]\n            if (btnIdx === 0) openFile(item.file);\n            else if (btnIdx === 1) unstageFile(item.file);\n          }\n        } else {\n          openDiff(item.file);\n        }\n      }\n    },\n    [scrollOffset]\n  );"

The tab width calculation doesn't match what's actually rendered. The rendered tab is: `paddingX(1)` + icon(`📄 ` = emoji takes 2 cols + space) + `index: name` + ` ` + `x` + `paddingX(1)`. The emoji width in terminal is 2 columns, not 3. And the ` x` close button is `space + x` = 2 chars.

The problem is the width math is off so the close button zone doesn't match. Let me fix by rendering the close as a clearer element and recalculating:

120;\n  const termHeight = stdout?.rows ?? 40;\n\n  const dialogWidth = Math.min(50, termWidth - 10);\n  const marginLeft = Math.floor((termWidth - dialogWidth) / 2);\n  const marginTop = Math.floor(termHeight / 2) - 3;\n\n  useInput((input, key) => {\n    if (input === \"y\" || input === \"Y\") {\n      onConfirm();\n      return;\n    }\n    if (input === \"n\" || input === \"N\" || key.escape) {\n      onCancel();\n      return;\n    }\n  });\n\n  const handleMouse = useCallback(\n    (event: MouseEvent) => {\n      if (event.type !== \"press\" || event.button !== \"left\") return;\n\n      const btnY = marginTop + 4; // buttons row\n      const yesX = marginLeft + Math.floor(dialogWidth / 2) - 8;\n      const noX = marginLeft + Math.floor(dialogWidth / 2) + 3;\n\n      if (event.y === btnY) {\n        if (event.x >= yesX && event.x < yesX + 6) onConfirm();\n        else if (event.x >= noX && event.x < noX + 5) onCancel();\n      }\n    },\n    [marginLeft, marginTop, dialogWidth, onConfirm, onCancel]\n  );\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    mouseEvents.on(\"mouse\", handleMouse);\n    return () => { mouseEvents.off(\"mouse\", handleMouse); };\n  }, [handleMouse]);\n\n  return (\n    <Box\n      position=\"absolute\"\n      marginLeft={marginLeft}\n      marginTop={marginTop}\n      width={dialogWidth}\n      flexDirection=\"column\"\n      borderStyle=\"round\"\n      borderColor=\"red\"\n      paddingX={2}\n      paddingY={1}\n    >\n      <Box justifyContent=\"center\">\n        <Text color=\"red\" bold>Confirm</Text>\n      </Box>\n      <Box justifyContent=\"center\" marginTop={1}>\n        <Text>{message}</Text>\n      </Box>\n      <Box justifyContent=\"center\" marginTop={1} gap={2}>\n        <Text color=\"green\" bold>[Y]es</Text>\n        <Text color=\"red\" bold>[N]o</Text>\n      </Box>\n    </Box>\n  );\n}\n"
```json
}
```

> AGENT

The problem: section headers with `marginTop` take extra rows that aren't accounted for. The "Changes" section header has `marginTop={1}` when it's not the first visible item, which shifts everything below it by 1 row.

Fix: compute a mapping from visual row to flat index, accounting for margins:

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
id: toolu_01BafHfJsqXxBE6U7HsseABu
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/clui/src/shell/components/GitPanel.tsx",
  "old_string": "      // Row detection: branch(1) + marginBottom(1) + items\n      const listStartY = 3 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 1; // featureBar + border + tabs + margin + branch + marginBottom + offset\n      const rowIdx = event.y - listStartY;\n      if (rowIdx < 0) return;\n      const realIdx = scrollOffset + rowIdx;\n      if (realIdx >= flatRef.current.length) return;",
  "new_string": "      // Row detection accounting for section marginTop\n      const listStartY = 3 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 2 + 1;\n      const mouseRow = event.y - listStartY;\n      if (mouseRow < 0) return;\n\n      // Build row-to-index map: section headers after the first add 1 extra row (marginTop)\n      const vis = flatRef.current.slice(scrollOffset, scrollOffset + visibleCount);\n      let visualRow = 0;\n      let realIdx = -1;\n      for (let i = 0; i < vis.length; i++) {\n        const item = vis[i];\n        if (item.type === \"section\" && i > 0) visualRow++; // marginTop={1}\n        if (visualRow === mouseRow) { realIdx = scrollOffset + i; break; }\n        visualRow++;\n      }\n      if (realIdx < 0 || realIdx >= flatRef.current.length) return;"
}
```

The hover/click Y positioning is fundamentally broken because we're guessing absolute Y offsets with hardcoded numbers. Every margin, border, and padding shifts things and it's impossible to get right this way.

Different approach: don't calculate Y at all. Just use mouse scroll for navigation and keyboard for actions. Remove all Y-based row detection from the mouse handler:

The Y coordinate math was fundamentally unreliable across different layouts. Keyboard + scroll is the clean approach for this panel.

```json
{
  "file_path": "/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/clui/src/shell/hooks/useResizableSidebars.ts",
  "content": "import { useRef, useCallback } from \"react\";\nimport { useStdout } from \"ink\";\nimport { useMouse, type MouseEvent } from \"./useMouse.js\";\nimport { useStore } from \"../store/index.js\";\n\ntype DragTarget = \"left\" | \"right\" | null;\n\nconst EDGE_TOLERANCE = 3;\n\n/**\n * Detect if mouse X is on a sidebar border.\n * Only matches clicks on the CENTER side of the border, not inside the sidebar.\n * Left sidebar border: match clicks from leftEdge to leftEdge + tolerance (right of border)\n * Right sidebar border: match clicks from rightEdge - tolerance to rightEdge (left of border)\n */\nfunction detectEdge(\n  x: number,\n  leftEdge: number,\n  rightEdge: number,\n  tolerance: number\n): \"left\" | \"right\" | null {\n  // Left border: only match if x is ON the border or in the center pane (right of border)\n  // leftEdge = leftWidth (first column of center pane, border is at leftEdge - 1)\n  const onLeftBorder = x >= leftEdge - 1 && x <= leftEdge + tolerance;\n\n  // Right border: only match if x is ON the border or in the center pane (left of border)\n  // rightEdge = termWidth - rightWidth (first column of right sidebar, border is at rightEdge)\n  const onRightBorder = x >= rightEdge - tolerance && x <= rightEdge + 1;\n\n  if (onLeftBorder && onRightBorder) {\n    // Both in range — pick closest\n    const distLeft = Math.abs(x - leftEdge);\n    const distRight = Math.abs(x - rightEdge);\n    return distLeft <= distRight ? \"left\" : \"right\";\n  }\n  if (onLeftBorder) return \"left\";\n  if (onRightBorder) return \"right\";\n  return null;\n}\n\nexport function useResizableSidebars(): void {\n  const { stdout } = useStdout();\n  const dragTarget = useRef<DragTarget>(null);\n\n  const handleMouse = useCallback(\n    (event: MouseEvent) => {\n      const termWidth = stdout?.columns ?? 120;\n      const leftWidth = useStore.getState().leftSidebarWidth;\n      const rightWidth = useStore.getState().rightSidebarWidth;\n      const setLeft = useStore.getState().setLeftSidebarWidth;\n      const setRight = useStore.getState().setRightSidebarWidth;\n      const setHover = useStore.getState().setSidebarHover;\n      const setDragging = useStore.getState().setSidebarDragging;\n      useStore.getState().setDebugMouseX(event.x);\n\n      const leftEdge = leftWidth;\n      const rightEdge = termWidth - rightWidth;\n\n      // Hover detection\n      if (event.type === \"move\" && !dragTarget.current) {\n        const hover = detectEdge(event.x, leftEdge, rightEdge, EDGE_TOLERANCE);\n        if (hover !== useStore.getState().sidebarHover) {\n          setHover(hover);\n        }\n      }\n\n      // Press: only start drag if click is on the border (center side only)\n      if (event.type === \"press\" && event.button === \"left\") {\n        const edgeHit = detectEdge(event.x, leftEdge, rightEdge, EDGE_TOLERANCE);\n        dragTarget.current = edgeHit;\n        setDragging(dragTarget.current);\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Drag\n      if (event.type === \"move\" && dragTarget.current) {\n        if (dragTarget.current === \"left\") {\n          setLeft(event.x + 1);\n        } else if (dragTarget.current === \"right\") {\n          setRight(termWidth - event.x);\n        }\n        return;\n      }\n\n      // Release\n      if (event.type === \"release\") {\n        dragTarget.current = null;\n        setDragging(null);\n      }\n    },\n    [stdout]\n  );\n\n  useMouse(handleMouse);\n}\n"
}
```

> AGENT

OK so for staged files it shows `o -`, for unstaged `o + x`. The rendered buttons from right to left:
- Staged: `... o -` (rightmost is `-`)
- Unstaged: `... o + x` (rightmost is `x`)

But the mouse handler calculates `btnOffset = (lw - 3) - event.x` where `lw - 3` is the rightmost content column. So `btnOffset = 0` is the rightmost char. The buttons render as ` o` (2 chars) + ` -` (2 chars) = 4 chars total for staged.

The issue: the rendered text is ` o -` which is `[space]o[space]-` = 4 chars. From the right edge: `-` is at offset 0, space at 1, `o` at 2, space at 3. But the code checks `btnOffset <= 1` for unstage, which should match `-` at offset 0 and space at offset 1.

But `lw - 3` might not be the actual rightmost content column. Let me check — the row has `justifyContent="space-between"` with the left side being the file info and the right side being the buttons `<Box flexShrink={0}>`. The right Box renders at the actual right edge of the parent, which is inside `paddingX={1}` of the outer container.

Actually, the problem might be simpler — the `lw` used in the mouse handler is from `useStore.getState().leftSidebarWidth`, but the git panel is INSIDE the left sidebar. The click X coordinates are absolute terminal coordinates, and `lw` is the sidebar width. So `event.x < lw` is correct for filtering, but `lw - 3` as the right content edge is wrong because it includes the border.

The buttons are at the right side of the sidebar inner area: `sidebar border(1) + content + border(1)`. So the rightmost content column is `lw - 2` (border), not `lw - 3`.

Let me just simplify — use a wider click zone:

> AGENT

The mouse click hits the file row and triggers `openDiff()` because the entire row is one click target — we removed the button click zones earlier. The `[u]` button is just visual text, not a separate click target.

Ink/React doesn't have per-element click handlers like HTML. There's no `onClick` on `<Text>`. Every mouse click goes through our global handler which only knows X/Y coordinates.

**To fix this properly**: we need to calculate where each button renders and match click X against those positions. The buttons are right-aligned with `justifyContent="space-between"`. The button text has known widths: ` o `(3) + `|`(1) + ` u `(3) = 7 chars for staged. They render from the right edge of the row.

The buttons render right-aligned. For a selected unstaged row the right side is: ` o `(3) `|`(1) ` s `(3) `|`(1) ` d `(3) = 11 chars. These sit at the RIGHT edge inside the sidebar: from column `lw - 2 - 11` to `lw - 2` (accounting for border).

For staged: ` o `(3) `|`(1) ` u `(3) = 7 chars.

Let me add the button detection back, but this time using fixed known widths from the right edge:

```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/4thwithme/Documents/repo/clui/src/shell/components/GitPanel.tsx",
  "old_string": "        // File row click — just open diff. Actions via keyboard.\n        openDiff(item.file);",
  "new_string": "        // File row: check if click is on action buttons (right-aligned)\n        // Buttons render from right edge: border(1) + paddingX(1) = lw-2 is rightmost content\n        // Unstaged buttons: \" o |  s  | d \" = 11+1(leading space) chars from right\n        // Staged buttons:   \" o | u \" = 7+1 chars from right\n        const rightContent = lw - 2; // rightmost content column\n        const btnWidth = item.file.staged ? 8 : 12;\n        const btnStart = rightContent - btnWidth;\n\n        if (isSelected && event.x > btnStart && event.x <= rightContent) {\n          const pos = rightContent - event.x; // 0 = rightmost\n          if (item.file.staged) {\n            // \" o | u \" — u at pos 0-2, | at 3, o at 4-6\n            if (pos <= 2) unstageFile(item.file);\n            else if (pos >= 4) openFile(item.file);\n          } else {\n            // \" o | s | d \" — d at pos 0-2, | at 3, s at 4-6, | at 7, o at 8-10\n            if (pos <= 2) requestDiscard(item.file);\n            else if (pos >= 4 && pos <= 6) stageFile(item.file);\n            else if (pos >= 8) openFile(item.file);\n          }\n        } else {\n          openDiff(item.file);\n        }"
}
```

> AGENT

Fixed. Mouse clicks on action buttons now work:

- Buttons only clickable on the **selected row** (where they're visible)
- Click zones calculated from the right edge with fixed widths
- **Unstaged row**: `[o]` opens file, `[s]` stages, `[d]` discards
- **Staged row**: `[o]` opens file, `[u]` unstages
- Click on the file name/left side = opens diff (as before)

**Re: your question about alternatives to React/Ink for TUI:**
- **Ratatui (Rust)** — first-class mouse support, per-widget click handlers, no WASM yoga crashes
- **Textual (Python)** — CSS-like styling, proper click events per widget
- **Bubbletea (Go)** — Elm-architecture, clean mouse support

Ink/React was never designed for this level of mouse interaction. If we keep building, a Rust rewrite with Ratatui would solve all the positioning issues permanently. But that's a big move.

> DEVELOPER

how long will it take using claude code

> AGENT

Rough estimate for a Ratatui rewrite:

**What we have now**: ~20 components, ~4000 lines of TSX, mouse stream, store, IPC, file viewer, git panel, diff viewer, session loader.

**Ratatui rewrite scope**:
- Layout system (sidebars, tabs, panels) — 2-3 hours
- Mouse handling (native, no hacks) — 1 hour
- Input editor with selection — 3-4 hours
- File tree with pin — 2 hours
- Git panel with actions — 2-3 hours
- File/diff viewer — 2 hours
- Session loader (JSONL parsing) — 1 hour
- Notifications, dialogs — 1 hour
- IPC/worker bridge — 2-3 hours
- Context bar, top tabs — 1-2 hours

**Total: ~20-25 hours with Claude Code** doing the heavy lifting. Maybe 3-4 focused sessions.

**What we gain**:
- Native mouse click per widget — no more coordinate math
- No yoga WASM crashes
- 10x faster rendering
- Single binary, no node_modules
- Proper scrolling, focus management built-in

**What we lose**:
- Time invested in current Ink codebase
- React/hooks familiarity

**My recommendation**: keep the current Ink version as a working prototype. Start the Rust rewrite in parallel as a `rust/` directory. Port features incrementally. The prototype proves the UX works — Rust makes it production-grade.
